title: From strategy to sustainable business performance: linking CSR and green transformational leadership with behavioral and organizational identification mechanisms in a crisis-affected setting
summary: Sustainability outcomes depend not only on organizational strategies but also on leadership behaviors and employee engagement, especially in crisis-affected economies. Drawing on stakeholder, transformational leadership, social exchange, and social identity theories, this study examines how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and green transformational leadership (GTL) relate to sustainable business performance (SBP) through organizational citizenship behavior for the environment (OCBE), with organizational identification (OI) as a moderator. Survey data collected between January and June 2025 from 500 employees and managers of Lebanese organizations participating in the United Nations Global Compact were analyzed using hierarchical structural equation modeling. CSR’s direct association with SBP was not supported in the combined model, and its indirect association through OCBE was not supported under the bootstrap confidence-interval criterion. GTL is directly and indirectly associated with SBP, and OI strengthens the GTL–OCBE link. Findings reposition leadership and employee identification as key pathways associated with sustainability outcomes in this crisis-affected context, offering theoretical and managerial implications.

title: Startups en Colombia y el Lienzo Canvas: Análisis de Casos
summary: i) Introducción: Este artículo examina un conjunto de startups colombianas bajo el modelo de lienzo Canvas (Business Model Canvas) elaborado por los autores a fin de comprender sus modelos de negocio en un entorno competitivo e innovador. ii) Objetivo: Analizar modelos de negocio de startups colombianas mediante el Business Model Canvas para evaluar su aplicabilidad en entornos innovadores. iii) Metodología: Tras una revisión bibliográfica, se estudian tres casos representativos: Rappi (entregas), GoPass (movilidad) y Addi (fintech). Los autores construyeron y analizaron sistemáticamente el Canvas de cada empresa. iv) Resultados El Canvas demostró ser una herramienta ágil y efectiva para visualizar y desglosar los modelos de negocio. El análisis permitió contrastar claramente sus propuestas de valor, segmentos de clientes, fuentes de ingreso y estructuras de costo, revelando patrones estratégicos adaptados a sus sectores. v) Conclusiones: El estudio valida el Canvas como instrumento práctico para el análisis estratégico en el ecosistema emprendedor. Los casos amplían el conocimiento sobre startups latinoamericanas y destacan la utilidad de herramientas visuales para la toma de decisiones en contextos competitivos dinámicos

title: Data Quality, AI Effectiveness, and Food Supply Chain Traceability: A Theory-Driven Framework for Resilience
summary: AI is becoming more used to improve the traceability and transparency of Moroccan food supply chains. Still, the efficiency of AI-powered traceability systems is strongly based on the quality of the data used. While research has flourished in the fields of AI, digital traceability, and supply chain resilience, the importance of data quality as an eminent antecedent of AI efficiency has not been adequately studied. This paper adopts a model-focused conceptual design, based on an integrative synthesis of complementary theoretical perspectives to reveal the varieties of ways through which the technical, semantic, and governance dimensions of a high-quality data contribute to improve AI analytical ability and the eventual realization of transparency, traceability, and resilience of the Moroccan food supply chain. Based on the theoretical lenses of Information Quality theory, the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Socio-Technical Systems theory, the setup regards AI effectiveness as a mediating factor and supply chain complexity and digital maturity as contextual factors which may impact the relationships. A set of research propositions specifies the proposed direct, mediating, and moderating relationships. The proposed framework is conceptual and has not yet been empirically validated; therefore, the proposed relationships should be interpreted as theoretically derived rather than empirically established. The paper contributes to the literature by integrating data quality, AI effectiveness, transparency, traceability, and resilience within a unified theoretical model and by positioning data quality as a strategic foundation for AIenabled supply chain capabilities. The framework provides a basis for future empirical validation in Moroccan food supply chain contexts.

title: Effect of OPay Microfinance Bank on Small and Medium Enterprises in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the effect of OPay Microfinance Bank on small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria, with particular emphasis on access to loan facilities and the quality and efficiency of financial services. Specifically, the study sought to examine the effect of OPay loan products (OKash and Easimoni) on SMEs’ access to loan facilities in Nigeria and determine the effect of OPay’s internet banking transaction success rate on SMEs’ access to financial services. Two research questions and corresponding hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. Relevant conceptual, theoretical, and empirical literature was reviewed. An ex post facto research design was adopted. Data were obtained from OPay’s annual reports, Central Bank of Nigeria publications, and publications of the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS). Descriptive statistics and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression were used to analyse the data. The findings revealed that OPay’s loan products had a statistically significant effect on SMEs’ access to loan facilities in Nigeria ( , ). Similarly, OPay’s internet banking transaction success rate had a statistically significant effect on SMEs’ access to financial services ( , ). The findings suggest that OPay’s loan products and transaction success rate are important factors associated with SME access to loans and financial services, although structural limitations may constrain the translation of digital financial access into broader financial empowerment. The study recommended that OPay strategically expand its loan product offerings to reach more underserved small businesses. It also recommended that regulatory authorities create an enabling environment for fintech-driven SME financing through proportionate regulation that balances innovation with consumer protection.

title: Mapping the Intellectual Landscape of CSR and Stakeholder Engagement: A Two-decade Bibliometric Review
summary: Corporate social responsibility and stakeholder engagement have emerged as critical areas of research in business and management studies, reflecting the growing emphasis on ethical business practices, sustainability and corporate governance. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of corporate social responsibility and stakeholder engagement research, examining 606 articles published in Scopus and Web of Science between 2004 and 2025. The analysis uncovers publication patterns, influential authors, top journals and citation networks, offering a systematic view of knowledge progression in the field. Further, through co-word analysis and thematic mapping, the study identifies core themes, highlighting emerging topics and outlining future directions.

title: THE EFFECT OF CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER POWER ON AUDIT QUALITY
summary: Prior research finds that Chief Financial Officer (CFO) characteristics can affect financial reporting quality and the firm's interaction with the auditor. The current study provides a broad examination of the effect of CFO power on audit quality. In this study, CFO power is measured using accounting or auditing expertise, tenure, and the CFO's formal position in the general meeting. Audit quality is examined through three observable outcomes: abnormal audit fees, modified audit opinions, and material financial statement misstatements. Based on a sample of 818 observations from companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange during 2015-2024, the results show that CFO power is associated with higher abnormal audit fees, a greater likelihood of receiving modified audit opinions, and a higher likelihood of material misstatements. These findings suggest that CFO power in the sample is more closely associated with increased auditor concern and financial reporting risk than with improved audit quality. The results emphasize the importance of CFO power in the financial reporting and auditing process and indicate that client-side characteristics can be reflected in audit pricing, final auditor judgments, and the quality of reported financial information.

title: THE DYNAMICS OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, TAX PLANNING, AND FIRM PERFORMANCE: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM LISTED COMPANIES ON THE STOCK EXCHANGE OF THAILAND, 2015–2024
summary: Background and Objectives: Corporate tax planning is a strategic decision with direct consequences for after-tax cash flows, investment capacity, and equity market valuation. This study examines three interrelated questions: (1) whether composite corporate governance (CG) scores predict tax planning intensity among listed companies; (2) whether tax planning predicts firm performance; and (3) whether CG moderates the tax planning–firm performance relationship. The study focuses on non-financial companies listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) during 2015–2024, a period spanning COVID-19 disruption, monetary-policy volatility, and sustained CG reforms under the IOD assessment system. Methods: An unbalanced panel of 2,702 firm-year observations from 349 non-financial SET-listed companies is analyzed using two-way fixed effects regression with firm-clustered standard errors. Two tax planning proxies—effective tax rate (ETR) and book-tax differences (BTD)—are deployed simultaneously. Five robustness checks probe the stability of all findings: lagged CG (R1), lagged BTD (R2), full-sample expansion with an unrated-firm dummy (R3), industry-adjusted ROA (R4), and two-way clustered standard errors (R5). Results: Three principal findings emerge. First, composite CG scores (IOD star-rating; mean = 4.21, SD = 0.78, range 3–5 stars) exhibit no statistically significant association with either ETR or BTD—consistent with institutional decoupling. Second, BTD is a robust positive predictor of ROA (β = 0.277, SE = 0.042, p < .001) and Tobin's Q (β = 0.971, SE = 0.409, p = .018), while ETR is non-significant across all specifications—a proxy-sensitivity finding with direct methodological implications for emerging-market research. Third, CG does not moderate the tax planning–performance relationship. All findings survive five robustness checks. Application of this study: For regulators (SEC/SET/IOD), the findings argue for integrating tax-specific governance criteria—board-level tax policy, audit committee tax expertise, and GRI Standard 207 disclosures—into CG assessments. Institutional investors should complement ETR with BTD in valuation frameworks. Corporate boards should formalize tax risk policies at board level to bridge the gap between formal CG compliance and substantive tax governance. Conclusions: Composite CG scores, as currently structured under Thailand's voluntary IOD assessment system, do not discipline corporate tax behavior—evidencing institutional decoupling attributable to score compression, voluntary-participation selection bias, and operational delegation of tax decisions below board level. BTD outperforms ETR as a tax planning proxy in this emerging-market setting. Thai equity investors interpret high BTD as a managerial capability signal rather than an opacity risk, consistent with the value creation hypothesis.

title: The Effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on The Financial Sustainability Of MSMES in Medan City
summary: This study examines the effect of Fintech Adoption and Digital Accounting on the Financial Sustainability of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Medan City. An associative quantitative design was applied to a survey of 120 MSME owners and managers in the culinary, fashion, retail trade, and service sectors, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met all validity and reliability criteria. Fintech Adoption had a positive and significant effect on Financial Sustainability (β = 0.412; t = 4.873; p < 0.001), and Digital Accounting also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.358; t = 4.126; p < 0.001). Together, the two variables explained 43.4% of the variance in Financial Sustainability, with medium effect sizes (f² = 0.236 and 0.178, respectively). The findings suggest that digital financial services and digital bookkeeping reinforce MSME financial sustainability, so support programs in Medan should promote both together rather than treating them as separate agendas

title: Organizational centralization of accounting functions and forward-looking disclosure quality: evidence from financial shared service centers
summary: This paper examines how the organizational centralization of accounting functions, an underexplored element of firms' reporting infrastructure, relates to the quality of forward-looking disclosures. Using novel hand-collected data on financial shared service center (FSSC) adoption among Chinese A-share listed firms, we document a robust and positive association between FSSC adoption and the accuracy of management earnings forecasts. These forecasts are also more specific, and capital markets react more strongly to them. Further analyses show that FSSC adoption is associated with shorter audit report lags and fewer subsequent financial restatements. The association between FSSC adoption and forecast accuracy is also stronger among firms with greater internal information frictions. These findings are consistent with the view that FSSCs improve managers' access to timely and reliable accounting information, thereby supporting more accurate forecasts. We also find that FSSC effectiveness is stronger among firms with greater digital capabilities and a stronger culture of unity, as well as among more mature FSSCs and those operating under multi-center structures. Our findings add to the literature on reporting infrastructure and disclosure quality and offer insights for firms and policymakers considering FSSC adoption as part of digital transformation strategies.

title: Factors Influencing Auditors’ Professional Scepticism in Financial Statement Audits: A Theoretical Review, Empirical Synthesis, and Conceptual Framework for the Audit Market in Hanoi
summary: Professional skepticism is universally recognized as the cornerstone of financial statement audits, directly governing an external auditor’s cognitive ability to recognize anomalies, evaluate contradictory evidence, and detect material misstatements arising from error or deliberate corporate fraud. Despite its formal codification in International Standards on Auditing and Vietnamese Standards on Auditing, skepticism remains an elusive behavioral construct in practice, frequently undermined by cognitive heuristics, environmental stressors, commercial conflicts of interest, and socio-cultural hierarchies. This paper presents an extensive, multi-layered literature review systematically grounded in foundational theoretical paradigms—specifically, Hurtt’s Trait-Based Model, Nelson’s State Determinants Model, Ajzen’s Theory of Planned Behavior, Role Stress Theory, and Agency Theory. Building upon this theoretical architecture, the paper synthesizes global and domestic empirical evidence across four primary determinant clusters: individual auditor attributes, internal audit firm quality controls and leadership, workload and budgetary pressures, and client-specific characteristics and corporate governance. Furthermore, this study bridges an acute research gap by situating these determinants within the institutional, commercial, and socio-cultural idiosyncrasies of Hanoi’s audit market—characterized by profound hierarchical deference, deep-seated informal relational networks, severe busy-season calendar compression, and stark operational disparities between international Big 4 networks and domestic non-Big 4 practices. Finally, this paper proposes an integrative conceptual framework comprising six testable propositions and delineates an empirical methodological roadmap to guide forthcoming inquiries and assist audit practitioners, regulatory bodies, and standard-setters in safeguarding audit quality and restoring capital market credibility.

title: The Effects of SAP Implementation on Administrative Staff at a Selected South African University of Technology: Developing the ERP Lifecycle–Employee Adaptation Framework (ELEAF)
summary: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions such as SAP represent a vital investment for organisations seeking to unify varied operational activities into integrated, data-driven platforms. In institutions of higher learning, the use of ERP systems is a crucial component of digital transformation efforts aimed at improving administrative efficiency, institutional governance, and competitive positioning. This article examines the impact of SAP ERP implementation on both organisational and employee dynamics for administrative staff at the Durban University of Technology (DUT), emphasising technostress, digital fatigue, employee well-being, and post-implementation adaptation within a constrained higher education environment. Utilising a desktop appraisal methodology, the study synthesises existing literature to demonstrate how decisions made in the pre-implementation and implementation phases consistently affect employee experiences and organisational outcomes post-implementation. The study indicates that attaining enduring ERP effectiveness requires continuous capacity development, cooperative implementation approaches, and employee-centered support frameworks. The research develops an interdisciplinary model by integrating socio-technical, psychological, capacity-building, and normalisation perspectives, thereby improving the understanding of the human factors involved in ERP deployment within higher education. The study introduces the ERP Lifecycle–Employee Adaptation Framework (ELEAF), which outlines the progressive escalation of technostress during the pre-implementation, implementation, and post-implementation phases, linking each stage to a pertinent theoretical mechanism and a set of organisational interventions. The findings indicate that inadequate training, limited organisational support, dependence on key users, and absence of employee engagement contribute to technostress, digital fatigue, reduced job satisfaction, and challenges in post-implementation adaptation. The study further demonstrates that decisions taken throughout the ERP lifecycle have enduring impacts on employee well-being and organisational effectiveness beyond the system's implementation. This highlights the tangible consequences for higher education institutions, stressing the importance of continuous training, institutional support, systematic information sharing, employee wellness initiatives, and staff-centric ERP management to enhance long-term value achievement. It consequently lays the groundwork for future research on the human dimensions of digital transformation in resource-constrained environments.

title: Company business processes: theoretical justification
summary: This article examines the theoretical foundations of the formation and functioning of a company's business processes within the context of a process-based approach to management. The relevance of the study stems from the persistent terminological and structural ambiguity surrounding the category «business process», which hinders the implementation of process-based management at enterprises with a functional structure. Using theoretical analysis, synthesis, comparison, and a systems approach, this article explores the content of a business process through its key characteristics: the presence of inputs and outputs, resource transformation, customer focus, and value creation. The role of business processes as an object of corporate planning, strategic management, and innovation-driven development is characterized. A three-level classification (core, supporting, and management processes) is proposed, with development processes identified as a distinct category. The need for systems analysis, modeling, and continuous improvement of business processes in the context of digital transformation of the economy is substantiated. It is concluded that the process-based approach serves as a theoretical and methodological foundation for enhancing a company's efficiency and competitiveness.

title: From Digital Accounting Capability to MSME Sustainability: The Mediating Role of Financial Reporting Quality and the Moderating Role of Financial Literacy
summary: Purpose - This study examined whether digital accounting capability was associated with the sustainability of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), and whether financial reporting quality and financial literacy served as a mediator and moderator, respectively. Methodology: An explanatory cross-sectional survey of 258 MSME managers in the Special Region of Yogyakarta and Central Java, Indonesia, was analyzed using structural equation modeling with LISREL. Six hypotheses covered direct, indirect, and interaction pathways. Results: Digital accounting capability was not significantly associated with financial reporting quality or MSME sustainability. Financial reporting quality was positively associated with sustainability (coefficient = 1.45; t = 9.57). Its indirect pathway from digital accounting capability was not significant (coefficient = −0.05; t = −1.31). Financial literacy did not significantly moderate the digital accounting capability–reporting quality relationship (coefficient = 0.01; t = 1.94), but the financial reporting quality × financial literacy interaction was significant and negative (coefficient = −0.02; t = −3.84). Contribution: The results distinguish digital accounting capability from the quality of accounting information and show that financial literacy did not uniformly strengthen the tested relationships. The cross-sectional estimates support associations, not causal claims.

title: Optimizing Agentic Artificial Intelligence to Improve Business Process Automation Efficiency through Modern Digital Technology
summary: In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation (BPA) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision-making tasks. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule-based automation by enabling adaptive problem-solving, real-time context awareness, and cross-system collaboration. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes. Because this is a literature-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains.

title: Tariff Uncertainty and Climate Imperatives: Strategies for Supply Chain Decarbonization in Asia
summary: As low-carbon manufacturing accelerates, Asian export economies face growing pressure from cross-border carbon rules and unilateral trade tariffs. Mechanisms such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), together with rising protectionism, have made supply chain emissions central to market access and competitiveness. This paper examines how tariff volatility interacts with climate mandates across Asian production networks and assesses three strategies: carbon-pricing alignment, regional value chain integration, and clean energy deployment in industrial clusters. It finds that without shared carbon accounting standards and transition finance; fragmented border measures may widen industrial disparities between advanced and developing Asian economies. The study highlights the need for cooperative trade-climate frameworks that balance competitiveness with deep decarbonisation across ASEAN and South East Asia.

title: Adoptability of PPP Models to Overcome Procurement Issues in Affordable Housing Projects
summary: Abstract Urbanization has caused severe housing issues related to affordability in urban areas. In Colombo, Sri Lanka, middle-income earners are more vulnerable to housing issues due to housing unaffordability and demand supply imbalances, and structural and distributional issues. However, public–private partnership (PPP) models have been successfully initiated in addressing urban housing affordability issues worldwide. Hence, this research aimed to investigate the adaptability of PPP models to overcome procurement issues in state-sector middle-income housing projects in Sri Lanka. The aim was accomplished via a three rounds of the Delphi approach by collecting data through semistructured interviews from experts. Collected data were analyzed through manual content analysis via three-phase coding. Findings revealed that PPP models, joint venture, concession, design–build–finance–operate–maintain (DBFOM), build–own–operate–transfer (BOOT), lease–develop–operate, design–build–finance–operate (DBFO), mixed PPP, and build-lease-transfer (BLT) offer viable alternatives for addressing challenges in delivery of affordable housing in Sri Lanka through conventional public-sector procurement methods. Key PPP features identified as critical to overcoming existing procurement issues include partnership and collaboration, shared risks and responsibilities, private funding, innovation and efficiency, value for money, and digital transformation. However, weak regulatory frameworks, lack of sector-specific PPP policies, bureaucratic inefficiencies, and absence of a central authority were highlighted as barriers to implementation of PPPs. The findings offer a foundation for countries that share similar socioeconomic backgrounds, particularly for developing countries, to consider PPP models in delivery of affordable housing.

title: Mapping Global Research Trends in Digital Transformation and Cyberpreneurship Through Bibliometric Analysis
summary: Digital transformation has become a major driver of change across various business sectors, including the rapid growth of cyberpreneurship in the digital economy era. The utilization of technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, and digital platforms enables entrepreneurs to create innovations and enhance their global competitiveness. However, research on digital transformation and cyberpreneurship remains fragmented and has not been systematically mapped, making it difficult to understand research trends, key focus areas, and existing gaps. Therefore, this study aims to map the development of research trends, intellectual structures, and major themes in the fields of digital transformation and cyberpreneurship. This study employs a bibliometric analysis method with a quantitative approach to scientific publications indexed in databases such as Scopus and Web of Science within a specified period. The data are analyzed using software tools such as VOSviewer to identify collaboration patterns, dominant keywords, and relationships among research topics. The findings indicate a significant increase in the number of publications related to these topics in recent years, reflecting the growing academic interest in digital transformation and cyberpreneurship. The main findings identify several major research clusters, including technological innovation, digital business strategies, consumer behavior, and startup ecosystems. Furthermore, the research focus has shifted from technical aspects toward strategic and policy-related dimensions. The study concludes that digital transformation plays a crucial role in fostering the growth of cyberpreneurship. However, significant research gaps remain, particularly in the context of developing countries and practical implementation aspects. Therefore, future studies are recommended to explore more contextual and sustainable approaches to support the inclusive development of digital entrepreneurship ecosystems.

title: International Evidence on the Relationship Between ESG Decoupling and Earnings Quality
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) decoupling and earnings quality (EQ) using an international sample of firms over the period 2005–2024. ESG decoupling refers to the misalignment between firms' ESG disclosure and ESG performance. The results show that ESG decoupling is negatively associated with EQ, suggesting that greater divergence between what firms communicate about ESG and what they substantively achieve is linked to lower‐quality financial reporting. This finding is consistent with legitimacy theory, which distinguishes between symbolic and substantive organisational behaviour. Further analysis shows that the negative association is stronger in countries with weaker governance quality, indicating that the institutional environment shapes the extent to which ESG misalignment is associated with reporting quality. Additional tests distinguishing between the direction of misalignment reveal that greenwashing is negatively associated with EQ, whereas brownwashing is not significantly associated with EQ. Overall, the findings extend the literature by showing that ESG decoupling is relevant to both the credibility of sustainability reporting and financial reporting quality, and that this association varies across governance settings.

title: Applications of operations research techniques in supply chain optimisation
summary: Supply chains involve linked decisions on facility location, production, inventory, routing and supplier choice under limits on capacity, cost and time. This paper reviews seventeen research papers on Operations Research (OR) in supply chains and compares the techniques they use: Linear and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (LP and MILP), metaheuristics (Genetic Algorithm and Tabu Search), Discrete-Event Simulation (DES), Economic Order Quantity (EOQ), Markov Decision Processes with Dynamic Programming (MDP and DP) and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), together with decomposition methods such as Benders decomposition and Lagrangian relaxation. Each technique is scored on six weighted criteria: decision quality, fit with network decisions, scalability, handling of uncertainty, implementation effort and documented impact. MILP ranks first, because it models yes or no structural choices and continuous flows together and returns optimal or provably near-optimal answers. Its weaknesses, problem size and uncertainty, are addressed in the literature through decomposition, stochastic extensions and simulation. We therefore recommend MILP as the core technique, supported by those tools, and we discuss gaps in the evidence and what we could have done better.

title: Human Capital and Digitalisation in FMCG Supply Chain for Sustainable Operations: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: The Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) business is under pressure to improve operational efficiency and solve sustainability issues in a digital world. Human capital and digitalisation drive productivity, responsiveness, and long-term competitiveness in sustainable operations. However, present research frequently isolate these elements, limiting knowledge of their combined impact. This PRISMA-guided Systematic Literature Review (SLR) examines human capital and digitisation in FMCG supply chains. Current research trends, theme insights, and knowledge gaps are reviewed. Data shows that AI, automation, predictive analytics, and the IoT boost efficiency, supply chain visibility, and decision-making. Adoption and use of these technologies require human capital, including digital skills, organisational learning, and human-machine collaboration. The analysis shows that FMCG contexts in emerging nations have underexplored human capital and digitalisation integration. The findings improve awareness of how human capital and digital capabilities support sustainable operations, and they show FMCG companies must integrate staff development with digital technology adoption. A detailed overview of their interplay and sustainable supply chain management research and practice directions are presented in this operations management paper

title: Eco‐Centric Leadership and Competitive Advantage in an Emerging Market: The Roles of Radical Innovation, Corporate Social Responsibility, and Organizational Resilience Using SEM – ANN
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental pressures and competitive uncertainty increasingly require firms in emerging markets to translate sustainability‐oriented leadership into tangible competitive value. Drawing on the resource‐based view, this study examines how eco‐centric leadership influences competitive advantage through radical innovation and corporate social responsibility (CSR), while considering organizational resilience as a boundary condition. Survey data from respondents in Pakistan's food manufacturing sector were analyzed using a hybrid partial least squares structural equation modeling–artificial neural network (PLS‐SEM–ANN) approach. The results reveal that eco‐centric leadership has a significant negative direct association with competitive advantage, whereas its indirect effects through radical innovation and CSR are positive and significant, indicating competitive or inconsistent mediation. Radical innovation emerges as the stronger mediating mechanism and the most important predictor of competitive advantage in the ANN analysis. Organizational resilience strengthens the positive relationship between radical innovation and competitive advantage but slightly weakens the CSR–competitive advantage relationship; both moderation effects are small. The study extends the resource‐based view by showing that eco‐centric leadership generates competitive value primarily through organizational resource‐conversion mechanisms rather than leadership orientation alone. For managers in emerging‐market firms, the findings highlight the strategic importance of translating environmental leadership priorities into innovation and responsible organizational practices while treating resilience as a complementary capability.

title: CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
summary: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Other limitations include insufficient semantic interoperability, inadequate model fidelity, inconsistent latency assessment, deployment evidence, and consideration of cybersecurity and human intervention. The field therefore needs architectures that integrates event-driven context management, federated twin models, scalable optimization, auditable decision services, and explicit uncertainty handling.

title: A novel cloud-enabled enterprise information systems framework for accelerating digital transformation strategies
summary: The co-evolution of micro-frontend UIs and backend microservices in cloud-native environments is complicated by UI–API semantic drift, dynamic workloads, and safe-deployment constraints. A tripartite agentic AI framework is introduced that combines reinforcement-learning (RL) agents for adaptive runtime control, large-language-model (LLM) synthesizers for automated artifact generation, and policy-as-code governors for security and compliance enforcement. The co-evolution process is formulated as a drift-aware Markov decision process, while Kubernetes-native traffic shifting supports progressive rollout and rollback. KubeSim was used for offline policy training; the reported performance results were obtained from live AWS EKS, Google GKE, and Azure AKS clusters. Across five benchmarks, the framework achieved a mean resolution success rate of 91.4%, compared with 62.0% for rule-based control, 71.1% for a controlled zero-shot LLM baseline, and 79.0% for partial RL. The framework also reduced normalized mean time to recovery by 80%, normalized change failure rate by 75%, and CPU utilization by 30 percentage points, while attaining a 98% audit pass rate. Component-removal and counterfactual-return analyses indicate complementary contributions from adaptive control, artifact synthesis, and policy enforcement. These results support the effectiveness, scalability, and governability of the framework for cloud-native enterprise digital transformation.

title: Turning ESG Into Inclusive Governance: Workforce Capabilities and Board Gender Diversity in GCC Firms
summary: ABSTRACT The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies have increasingly integrated sustainability, corporate governance reform and social inclusion into their economic diversification agendas. Drawing on a strategic sustainability perspective, this study examines whether ESG performance contributes to inclusive governance by enhancing board gender diversity in publicly listed GCC firms. Specifically, it investigates workforce quality as a mediating mechanism and assesses the moderating roles of CSR strategy and sustainability‐linked executive compensation incentives. The study uses firm‐level ESG and financial data from London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Datastream, together with macroeconomic indicators from the World Bank, covering an unbalanced panel of 1398 firm‐year observations from 281 listed firms over the period 2010–2024. The data are analysed using two‐step system generalised method of moments (System‐GMM) estimation to account for dynamic persistence, unobserved heterogeneity and potential endogeneity while testing the proposed mediation and moderation relationships. The findings reveal that ESG performance is positively associated with both workforce quality and board gender diversity. However, workforce quality fully mediates the ESG‐board gender diversity relationship, indicating that ESG commitments are translated into inclusive board outcomes primarily through stronger human capital practices, employee‐oriented systems and inclusive organisational capabilities. The results further show that CSR strategy strengthens workforce quality but weakens the marginal effect of ESG performance on workforce outcomes, suggesting a substitution effect when CSR practices become highly formalised. Similarly, sustainability‐linked executive incentives directly support board gender diversity but reduce the positive influence of workforce quality on board gender diversity. Overall, the findings suggest that ESG performance alone is insufficient to advance gender‐inclusive governance unless supported by substantive workforce development and well‐aligned sustainability incentives. This study contributes to the CSR, ESG and sustainability governance literature by identifying workforce capabilities as a key organisational pathway linking ESG commitments to board‐level diversity outcomes in emerging GCC markets.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Sustainability, and Innovation: A Roadmap for the Digital Economy
summary: Abstract The rapid expansion of the digital economy has positioned artificial intelligence (AI) as both a transformative enabler of sustainability and a significant contributor to environmental degradation. This paper examines the dual role of AI within the digital economy, analyzing how intelligent automation, machine learning, and data-driven innovation can advance sustainable development while simultaneously creating new ecological burdens through energy-intensive computation, hardware proliferation, and electronic waste. Drawing on recent scholarship from the International Energy Agency, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, and peer-reviewed academic literature, this study synthesises evidence across three domains: the environmental costs of AI infrastructure, the potential of AI to accelerate progress toward the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and the emergence of Green AI as a disciplinary movement. The paper proposes a roadmap for reconciling innovation with sustainability, centred on energy-efficient algorithm design, circular economy integration, renewable energy procurement for data centres, and robust policy governance. The findings suggest that without deliberate intervention, the environmental footprint of AI will undermine the very sustainability objectives it promises to advance, making proactive stewardship an imperative for researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders alike. title: The Impact of Supply Chain Finance Digitalization on Corporate Working Capital Management Efficiency
summary: As firms face volatile cash flows, tighter external financing, and greater pressure to coordinate financial and operating activities, supply chain finance digitalization is changing how transaction data, financing, payments, and settlement are connected. Existing studies often examine digital supply chain finance through individual financial outcomes or isolated cases, while relatively few systematically consider both its direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms on working capital management efficiency. This paper examines the effect of digital supply chain finance on corporate working capital management efficiency through a structured review and conceptual synthesis of recent literature, with a focus on direct effects and three indirect mechanisms. The evidence suggests that digital supply chain finance improves working capital efficiency by accelerating financing and settlement, reducing unnecessary capital tied up in receivables and inventories, and coordinating receivables, payables, inventories, and cash flows. Overall, the main channels are greater information transparency, better financing access, and closer financial-operational coordination. This paper constructs an analytical framework that incorporates direct effects and multiple indirect transmission mechanisms. Thereby contributing to the literature on digitalization in supply chain finance and corporate working capital management.

title: Technological Advancements and Barriers in Adopting Digital Twins for Supply Chain Management
summary: Digital twins are expected to improve supply chain decisions by linking physical operations with models that simulate and optimize them. This literature review, guided by PRISMA 2020, analyzes 104 studies (2016 to 2026) on the enabling technologies of supply chain digital twins, the barriers to their adoption and the algorithmic evidence behind them. The studies were classified into evidence tiers by application domain; twelve supply chain studies and six algorithm studies from other sectors were coded by decision problem, algorithm family, integration level and validation, and the methodological quality of fifteen of them was appraised. The Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, cloud and edge computing, extended reality and blockchain are the main enablers, but in the analyzed set the supply chain evidence is largely conceptual: only two supply chain studies apply an algorithm, none implements a bidirectional digital twin, and only one reports performance measures from a model run. State estimation, reduced-order models and reinforcement learning, which would allow real-time operation, have been evaluated only in other sectors. Technical, organizational and economic barriers appear to reinforce each other. We propose a three-stage implementation pathway and an agenda of seven research gaps, including closed-loop integration, shared benchmarks and multi-company data governance.

title: Can linguistic vagueness in annual reports predict supply chain risk?
summary: Annual reports serve as a critical information channel for corporate stakeholders, especially for supply chain partners. We argue that linguistic vagueness in these reports can function as an early-warning signal for predicting supply chain risk. To test our proposition, we develop a theory-grounded measure of linguistic vagueness by integrating communication vagueness theory with the Word2Vec method. Our analysis of publicly listed companies in China reveals a robust positive association between linguistic vagueness and subsequent supply chain risk. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that this predictive capacity varies under different reputational pressures. Furthermore, by employing interpretable machine learning approaches within an out-of-sample predictive framework, we validate the consistent directional predictive signal via SHAP analysis and solidify the indicator’s predictive robustness. Ultimately, this study establishes linguistic vagueness as an incremental signal that carries significant out-of-sample predictive value for supply chain risk, providing stakeholders with a data-driven approach for proactive risk monitoring.

title: The North American germanium supply chain: military applications and civilian competition
summary: Germanium is not mined as a primary ore anywhere in North America. It comes out as a trace byproduct of zinc processing, at concentrations low enough that its supply follows the economics of zinc rather than germanium. Additionally, it depends on whether a smelter operator is willing to install a costly recovery circuit on top of ordinary zinc refining. That fact, more than any single company's decision, explains why a metal essential to night vision optics, thermal weapon sights, laser rangefinders, and satellite solar arrays runs through a chain that reduces to a small number of US zinc operations feeding one foreign smelter.

title: Digital transformation of marketing communications in the private healthcare market
summary: The article examines the specific characteristics of the private healthcare services market and highlights the significant role of digital marketing communications in building patient relationships and enhancing patient satisfaction. To identify the key factors determining the competitiveness of private medical clinics in Yekaterinburg, the competitive environment was analyzed using Porter’s Five Forces framework. The analysis revealed a high degree of supplier bargaining power, intense intra-industry competition, and significant buyer power, represented by patients. A set of strategic measures aimed at mitigating these risks is proposed, including the development of physician brands; partnerships with medical equipment manufacturers and the implementation of proprietary digital solutions; loyalty programs and personalized health check-ups; the development of evidence-based content marketing; positioning the medical facility as a center of expert diagnostics; and personalization of patient interactions. A survey was conducted to identify patients’ preferred communication channels with medical clinics. Based on the findings, a framework for distributing content across digital platforms is proposed. The results of the study provide a basis for developing recommendations for attracting new patients and strengthening the trust of existing patients in private healthcare providers.

title: The Influence of Organizational Culture Factors on the Acceptance of New Accounting Technology Among Accounting Staff in Foreign-Invested Enterprises in Hanoi City
summary: This paper examines the influence of organizational culture factors on the acceptance of new accounting technology among accounting staff in foreign direct investment (FDI) enterprises in Hanoi City, using a desk-research approach that combines synthesis, analysis, evaluation, and comparison of the literature. Drawing on Hofstede's theory of organizational culture, the Technology Acceptance Model, the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology, and Diffusion of Innovation theory, the paper develops a conceptual framework that clarifies the mechanisms through which five dimensions of organizational culture, namely power distance, uncertainty avoidance, individualism and collectivism, long-term and short-term orientation, and masculinity and femininity, affect the components of technology-acceptance behavior. The analysis shows that power distance and uncertainty avoidance play a relatively consistent role in amplifying social influence, while the interplay between parent-company culture and local culture within this type of enterprise adds a further layer of complexity to the digital transformation of accounting. Building on these findings, the paper proposes managerial implications tailored to each cultural dimension for enterprise managers, while also suggesting policy directions through which state management agencies can support digital transformation in the accounting profession.

title: Transitioning to Circular Automotive Systems: A Systematic Review of Supply Chain Practices and Implementation
summary: The Automobile industry shifts from linear to circular economy for sustainability on a global level with respect to the industrial revolution 5.0, but it faces challenges when establishing circular economy.Circular supply chain implementation is dependent on multiple barriers and enablers, including economic managerial, technological, regulatory and social domains, making it ineffective for single factor solution.The purpose behind this review is to conduct a systematic literature review to develop an understanding how these interconnected barriers and enablers can together shape the circular supply chain implementation and their performance, specifically inside the automotive sector which is still remain a little known.By applying the PRISMA framework on 150 peer reviewed articles, research papers.The research shows that literature focuses on primarily on electric vehicle barriers within developing economies.Circular supply chain implementation is governed not only by isolated barriers but by complex systematic interdependencies between enablers as well.This interdependencies are of enablers and barriers can be further classified into economical and financial, managerial and organizational, technological and infrastructure, policy and regularity and market and social.The study shows two systematic patterns, driving the transition technology-policy interdependence and conflicting relationship between large scale production and value extraction.The findings also presented a research agenda focusing on strategic value creation through material streams of automotive electronics, plastics and composites with high potential value and further insights are needed.Circular supply chain as a strategic approach for securing critical material supplies, while policymakers could leverage the use of digital tools as the foundational infrastructure for subsidies allocation and prevent the fraud.

title: Leeches and linchpins: a scoping review of seafood market intermediaries in small-scale fishery supply chains
summary: Abstract Seafood market intermediaries, often termed middlemen, play a crucial yet contested role in connecting small-scale fisheries (SSF) to global seafood markets. While their influence has long been recognized, scholarly accounts have tended to frame these intermediaries as either exploitative actors who constrain fishers’ livelihoods or as essential actors who provide access to markets, finance, and social protection. This scoping review examines how recent literature (2019–2021) normatively frames seafood market intermediaries, and what these framings reveal about scholarly and policy discourses on SSF. Using a qualitative synthesis of peer-reviewed and grey literature, we identify predominant framings that cast these intermediaries as both leeches and linchpins, thereby reinforcing power asymmetries while also buffering fishers against economic and social risks. We discuss how these normative framings shape broader narratives that influence fisheries governance and policy, with implications for equitable outcomes. The paper also demonstrates the value of systematic scoping methods for synthesizing qualitative marine social science research and provides methodological reflections for small research teams. Recognizing the diverse, gendered, and socially embedded roles of intermediaries can inform more just and context-sensitive interventions in SSF seafood supply chains.

title: The Evolution of Sharia Non-Compliance Risk (SNC) in the Digital Banking Ecosystem: A Bibliometric Analysis (2020-2026)
summary: This study aims to map the intellectual evolution and dynamics of literature on sharia non-compliance risk in the digital banking ecosystem. The method used is bibliometric analysis by extracting data from the Google Scholar database which is then visualized using VOSviewer software to identify trends, novelties, and interconnectedness between variables during the 2020–2026 period. The results of the study indicate the existence of seven main, interconnected discourse clusters, namely: digital transformation and the fintech ecosystem, strategic risk management of SNC, implementation of future technologies (Blockchain and AI), and strengthening digital sharia governance and audits. Key findings indicate that the resilience of sharia compliance in the digital era is greatly influenced by the risk mutation from administrative errors to algorithm-based systemic risks, which requires strengthening automated sharia audits through a Sharia-by-Design approach. The implications of this study provide a strategic foundation for regulators and banking practitioners in mitigating SNC risks through the integration of sharia parameters into information technology infrastructure to face the complexity of real-time transactions in the future.

title: ESG-INVESTMENT OF KAZAKHSTAN'S ENDOWMENT FUNDS: INSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS AND MECHANISMS TO OVERCOME THEM
summary: The study aims to identify and systematise the regulatory, financial, economic, organisational, and managerial constraints in Kazakhstan's endowment funds' transition to ESG investment, and to substantiate mechanisms for overcoming them. The methodological basis includes documentary and comparative legal analysis, an institutional approach, a comparative study of public examples, and scenario financial modelling. The regulatory framework has been analysed as of October 1, 2026. The analysis found that creating special legislation on endowment capital and developing national infrastructure for sustainable financing create institutional prerequisites for ESG investment but do not automatically ensure the implementation of relevant practices. The study identified limitations related to the permissibility of financial instruments, the certainty of the investment mandate, the quality of ESG information, professional competencies, and administrative costs. Scenario calculations for conditional funds with capital of 50, 100, and 500 million tenge showed that the financial availability of ESG procedures depends on asset scale. With a notional cost of 1.20 million tenge, the estimated coverage limits were 80 million tenge in the positive scenario and 240 million tenge in the negative scenario. Comparing institutional examples from Almaty, Astana, and the Karaganda region made it possible to identify differences in management tasks at certain stages of fund development. The scientific novelty lies in the development of an analytical model of the ESG transition, combining the legal admissibility of investments, financial capabilities, and organisational readiness. The practical significance of the results depends on their potential use in developing investment declarations, regulating interactions with management companies, and forming a control system. The limitations of the study are due to the lack of a comparable database of financial and portfolio indicators of endowment funds in Kazakhstan.

title: THE EFFECT OF KEY AUDIT MATTERS (KAM) DISCLOSURE, AUDIT COMMITTEE, COMPANY COMPLEXITY, AND RELATED- PARTY TRANSACTIONS ON AUDIT FEES
summary: This study aims to empirically examine and analyze the influence of Key Audit Matters (KAM) disclosure, audit committees, firm complexity, and related-party transactions on audit fees within the energy sector. The research employs a quantitative approach using panel data regression analysis. Through a purposive sampling technique, 91 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) were identified as the population for the 2022–2024 study period. A final sample of 36 companies was selected, resulting in 108 total observations. The findings indicate that audit committees and firm complexity have a significant positive impact on audit fees for energy sector companies, whereas Key Audit Matters (KAM) and related-party transactions do not show a significant influence. These results imply that public accounting firms (KAP) consider firm complexity and the presence of an audit committee as key determinants when setting audit fees for their clients. Furthermore, the findings suggest that the implementation of KAM disclosure requirements has been successfully integrated without imposing additional costs; however, they also highlight the need for ongoing oversight regarding the risks associated with related-party transactions, which may not yet be fully reflected in the determination of audit fees within the energy sector. This research contributes to a better understanding of how Key Audit Matters, audit committees, firm complexity, and related-party transactions affect audit fees for energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

title: AGENT-BASED SIMULATION OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REFORMS’ IMPACT ON BOARD DECISION-MAKING DYNAMICS AND RISK MITIGATION
summary: Purpose. Corporate governance reforms such as majority board independence, separation of the chief executive officer (CEO) and chair roles, board diversity requirements and dedicated risk committees are usually evaluated through firm-level outcome regressions that cannot observe the boardroom process through which reforms are expected to work. This study opens that process by modelling board decision-making as the emergent product of interacting director agents. Design/methodology/approach. An agent-based model (ABM) is developed and documented using the Overview, Design concepts and Details (ODD) protocol. A nine-member board, comprising a CEO, independent directors and executive insiders, evaluates a stream of CEO-sponsored proposals that carry both value and tail risk. Directors receive noisy and partly correlated signals, deliberate through status-weighted opinion updating with selective voice, and vote. Six governance scenarios are simulated across 2,000 boards and 100 proposals each under a normal and a stressed risk regime, supported by an independence sweep, a diversity-by-independence factorial experiment, a Latin hypercube global sensitivity analysis of 1,500 parameter combinations and board-size robustness checks. Findings. Under the baseline (CEO duality, three of eight non-CEO seats independent, a homogeneous board and no risk committee), boards reached the correct decision on 69.1 per cent of proposals and approved 66.6 per cent of value-destroying proposals. Separating the CEO and chair roles was the single most effective reform, raising accuracy to 79.0 per cent (Cohen’s d = 2.22). Majority independence, diversity and a risk committee each produced smaller gains of 1.4 to 2.6 percentage points. The combined package raised accuracy to 83.3 per cent and reduced tail-loss events by 21.5 per cent, rising to 37.1 per cent under stressed conditions. Reform benefits were sub-additive, the value of a risk committee roughly doubled under stress, and the gains came at the cost of 37 per cent longer deliberation and a small rise in the rejection of value-creating proposals. Global sensitivity analysis identified CEO duality and CEO optimism bias as the dominant drivers of both decision accuracy and tail losses. Originality/value. The study provides a transparent, replicable computational laboratory that links governance reforms to the micro-mechanisms of board deliberation, explains why reforms that change board composition without changing boardroom power deliver modest effects, and offers regulators and boards a basis for sequencing reforms.

title: Disclosed Tax Dispute Exposure and Accrual-Based Earnings Management: Evidence from Brazil
summary: Brazilian listed firms report material and persistent tax disputes in a setting that requires recurring judgment about recognition and disclosure and includes an observable premium listing regime. Using 3544 firm-year observations for 254 non-financial firms listed on B3 from 2009 to 2024, we examine whether accrual-based earnings management (AEM), measured as the absolute residual from a pooled Jones-family accrual model augmented with lagged return on assets, is associated with disclosed tax dispute exposure (DTE), measured as recognized tax provisions plus disclosed contingent tax liabilities scaled by total assets, and whether the association differs by Novo Mercado status. The performance control reduces the risk of classifying normal profitability-related accruals as abnormal, while the absolute value captures deviations in either direction; AEM remains a reporting-outcome proxy rather than a direct measure of internal-control effectiveness. In the primary fully interacted specification, the AEM slopes are 0.023 (SE 0.266) among firms outside and 0.093 (SE 0.068) among Novo Mercado firms; their difference is 0.070 (SE 0.274). The 95% confidence interval for the outside-segment slope [−0.498, 0.545] includes estimates from restricted models, indicating limited precision rather than evidence of no association. Sensitivity analyses using winsorized DTE and ln(1 + DTE) yield modest positive slopes in both groups but no precisely estimated group difference; restricting the sample to DTE ≤ 1 yields a positive outside-segment slope but an imprecise difference. Secondary between-firm and quantile models yield negative interactions, whereas the within-firm slope among Novo Mercado firms is positive. These estimator-specific patterns show that the AEM–DTE relation depends on the estimand and model restrictions and do not support a uniform governance-moderation, causal, or out-of-sample predictive interpretation.

title: Executive incentives and digital transformation: governance evidence from China
summary: Purpose This study examines how executive incentive structures align with the temporal and motivational demands of corporate digital transformation (DT), focusing on cash compensation, equity-based incentive exposure, and internal pay dispersion. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 3,583 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2023 (37,274 firm-year observations), we measure DT with a text-based annual-report index and estimate fixed-effects models supplemented by robustness, temporal, and endogeneity analyses. Findings Equity-based incentive exposure and internal pay dispersion are positively associated with DT, whereas the association between cash compensation and broad DT is weaker and more specification-sensitive. Internal pay dispersion exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with DT, suggesting that moderate tournament incentives may mobilize managerial effort, while excessive dispersion may weaken coordination. Complementary analyses show that cash compensation is positively associated with more immediate technology-oriented resource commitments. Practical implications Boards should match incentive structures to strategic time horizons. Cash rewards may support near-term resource mobilization, equity-based exposure is better aligned with delayed value creation, and pay dispersion should be calibrated to preserve motivation without undermining collaboration. Originality/value This study advances an incentive–strategy fit perspective by showing that executive incentives differ in temporal horizon and motivational mechanism. Equity-based exposure addresses temporal misalignment, while internal pay dispersion mobilizes effort and change subject to coordination costs.

title: Global Value Chains, Resilience and Strategic Behaviour
summary: In addressing risks to value chains, the choice of policy instrument matters and depends on institutional context. The role of fiscal policy in strengthening supply chain resilience has received increasing attention in recent years. We present empirical insights from India by estimating the extent of (critical) import dependencies for sectors like electrical machinery and equipment; machinery and mechanical appliances; organic chemicals; inorganic chemicals among others. In response to disruption risks affecting value chains, fiscal instruments could support resilience in multiple ways. In this paper we develop a game theoretic model to capture the industrial policy choices of the Government and firm’s production decision when cross-border supply chain disruption risk is a reality. The model internalises the social cost of import dependence through Government’s action that competitive markets fail to internalise. The government may use production-linked subsidy that supports output or an infrastructure-type subsidy that expands domestic productive capacity in situation of disruption of external origin. Since, such disruptions are increasingly a reality with varying probabilities, the model establishes that industrial policies should ideally involve both instruments.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Supply Chain Management: Applications, Evidence, Implementation Constraints, and Future Directions
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly investigated as decision-support technologies for supply chain management (SCM), yet their value depends on the nature of the decision, data availability, organisational capability and the methods used to evaluate outcomes. This critical narrative review examines applications across demand forecasting, inventory planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, risk management and sustainability. It brings together relevant peer-reviewed reviews, conceptual contributions and empirical studies, and distinguishes evidence from operational deployments from results reported in literature syntheses or simulations. The literature supports the practical relevance of data-driven prediction, pattern detection and decision augmentation, but it does not establish uniform improvements in cost, forecast accuracy, resilience or environmental performance across settings. Reviewed research also identifies integration costs, fragmented data, process misalignment, model drift, limited transparency and governance concerns as barriers to realising benefits. Recent work on generative AI broadens possible applications to document-intensive processes, synthetic scenarios and interactive decision support, while indicating that field-based validation remains limited. A process-oriented framework is proposed in which analytics inform planning, procurement, manufacturing, distribution and inventory decisions under continuous human oversight. The review argues that useful evaluations should compare AI-supported decisions against relevant operational baselines, account for service levels and cost trade-offs, and document transferability across sectors and resource settings. Future research should prioritise longitudinal field studies, cross-organisational coordination, responsible deployment and context-sensitive applications in emerging economies.

title: PERAN CSR MEMODERASI PENGARUH FINANCIAL DISTRESS DAN COMPANY GROWTH TERHADAP ERC
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Financial Distress (FD) and Company Growth (CG) on the Earnings Response Coefficient (ERC), as well as the moderating role of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure in state-owned enterprises (SOEs) listed on the IDX during 2018–2023. Using a quantitative associative approach and purposive sampling, a final sample of 17 SOEs (102 panel observations) was obtained. Data were analyzed using Random Effect Model panel regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results show that FD (proxied by Altman Z-score) has a statistically significant positive coefficient, which economically proves that higher Financial Distress (lower Z-score) leads to a lower ERC. Conversely, CG has no significant effect on ERC due to high leverage financing asset expansion. CSR does not moderate the FD–ERC relationship (acting as a predictor moderator). However, CSR significantly moderates (quasi-moderator) the CG–ERC relationship (+2.446; p = 0.001), strengthening and transforming an insignificant asset growth signal into a positive market-appreciated signal. These findings confirm that CSR serves as a strategic tool that enhances the credibility of SOE growth in capital markets. Keywords: CSR, ERC, FG and CG.

title: Digital Transformation in Language Teaching: From Traditional Methods to Artificial Intelligence
summary: This article examines the digital transformation of language teaching and analyses the impact of contemporary digital technologies and artificial intelligence on the language-teaching process. It focuses on the evolution of traditional forms of instruction, the potential of digital educational technologies, and the main areas where artificial intelligence is applied in language teaching. The advantages of using intelligent systems are examined, including the personalisation of instruction, the automation of instructional guidance, increased access to educational resources, and opportunities for online learning. The article identifies the main risks to academic integrity. It addresses issues of information reliability, the protection of learners’ personal data, and the preservation of the teacher’s leading role in the educational process. Contemporary scholarly works related to the subject have been examined. Based of an analysis of the theoretical literature on the issues under investigation, the article demonstrates the need of integrate artificial intelligence technologies harmoniously into language education while preserving education’s humanistic orientation of education and recognising the importance of the teacher’s role as a mentor and facilitator. It is concluded that the most promising model for the development of contemporary language education is one based on collaboration between the teacher and artificial intelligence. Such a model contributes to improving the quality of instruction, developing communicative competence, saving time and human resources, and fostering learners’ digital skills.

title: AI-Driven Personalisation in Digital Payments: Examining Its Impact on Customer Trust
summary: Abstract Digital India programme over a decade shown an upward performance by setting a benchmark. It is a flagship initiatives of the Government of India. It has digitally empowering the society and digital economy. Digital economy is an economic activities enhanced with the digital transformation using the digital computing tools. It provided various opportunities in the Banking and Fintech sectors. In current scenario Artificial Intelligence (AI) playing a very significant pivotal role by integrating the technology in all the sectors. It is enhancing the opportunities for the service provider and customer. Due to the rapid expansion of digital payment ecosystems, it has transformed the way how a consumers conduct their everyday financial transactions for purchasing their requirements either through online shopping i.e. e-commerce or visiting the store personal and using the digital banking or digital payment. In India, the digital payment especially using Unified Payments Interface (UPI) now has become a very important component of the digital financial ecosystem. Alongside this growth, the payment service providers are progressively integrating with the Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to personalise their customer experiences. This is providing an enhance features through transaction recommendations to the customers with amazing discount features or offers in the payments using the digital payments. It further enables the customers in identifying their spending insights and intelligent alerts and adaptive customer support. This conceptual research proposes to examine the relationship between AI driven personalisation and customer trust in digital payment systems. The study propose to integrate from the perspectives of adopting the model Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) with the trust theory. The proposed model considers AI personalisation, perceived usefulness, perceived relevance, transparency as among the key explanatory variables, with customer trust as the principal dependent construct. Behavioural intention and continuance intention are considered as potential outcomes of trust. The expected findings may provide very useful insight in the domain of digital banking, digital payment segment of the banks, fintech companies, and payment service providers to improve the trustworthy for the customer and responsible AI enabled payment ecosystems. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, AI-driven personalisation, digital payments, UPI, customer trust.
