title: Digitalization is More Than Just a Trend: Modernizing Financial Reporting in the Halal MSME Ecosystem of the Riau Islands
summary: This study examines the modernization of financial reporting among MSMEs in Riau Islands Province, focusing on Ayuraskitchen, a home-based business in Batam City that has grown into a multi-outlet cake business. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, the study analyzes the gradual transition in financial reporting from manual records and Microsoft Excel templates to the Lamikro application and, ultimately, the digital accounting application Mekari Jurnal. The findings indicate that modernization occurred gradually in accordance with the growth and needs of the business and was supported by consistent record-keeping, government training and assistance, and the availability of accessible technology. The implementation of digital financial reporting improved the organization, efficiency, and accessibility of financial information, while supporting cash flow monitoring and faster business decision-making. Systematic financial records also help MSMEs prepare financing documentation and improve their bankability by providing more structured business information, although access to financing is influenced by other factors. The study recommends strengthening accounting and digital literacy, providing continuous assistance, implementing SAK EMKM, and fostering collaboration among MSMEs, local governments, financial institutions, and financial technology providers to accelerate the modernization of MSME financial reporting.

title: DEVELOPING A GOVERNANCE COMPETENCE FRAMEWORK FOR VIETNAMESE UNIVERSITIES: BRIDGING THE AUTONOMY–COMPETENCE GAP IN DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: This study investigates the autonomy–competence gap in the Vietnamese higher education sector by developing a governance competence framework for universities operating under expanding institutional autonomy and accelerating digital transformation. Existing governance frameworks tend to examine formal structures or isolated managerial capabilities, but they do not adequately explain how universities in transitional systems convert regulatory autonomy into effective institutional practice. A qualitative research design was employed, drawing upon Vietnamese legal and policy documents, institutional governance materials from eight purposively selected universities, and semi-structured interviews with 23 participants comprising university leaders, policy officials, and governance scholars. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis supported by NVivo, combining deductive coding informed by governance, competency, institutional, and digital transformation theories with inductive identification of emerging themes. The findings reveal that although formal institutional autonomy has expanded significantly, uneven governance capacity across institutions constrains its effective implementation. Four interrelated governance competence domains emerged: Strategic and Policy Leadership, Financial and Human Resource Management, Digital Governance and Innovation, and Accountability and Assurance Culture. Interview evidence further highlights persistent challenges, including weak strategic governance, inflexible administrative and human resource structures, limited digital governance readiness, and an enduring compliance-oriented accountability mindset. The study demonstrates that institutional autonomy should be understood not merely as regulatory decentralisation but as a multidimensional organisational capability requiring balanced development across interconnected governance domains. It further argues that effective governance reform entails a fundamental transition from a compliance-focused accountability approach, centred on procedural adherence and documentation, to a quality-oriented governance culture that emphasises continuous improvement, transparency, evidence-based decision-making, and organisational learning. By conceptualising governance competence as the institutional capability that links formal autonomy with substantive organisational effectiveness and facilitates this shift from compliance to quality, this research advances higher education governance scholarship and proposes an integrated framework for institutional self-assessment, governance capacity building, and future empirical investigation of governance reform in transitional higher education systems.

title: Time-Series modeling of supply chain disruption drivers in ASEAN agri-food logistics networks
summary: Disruptions in agri-food supply chains pose logistical and operational challenges for ASEAN member economies, whose agricultural sectors are simultaneously exposed to fluctuations in freight costs and climate-related production shocks. Prior time-series applications in shipping markets, agricultural commodity co-movement, and supply chain performance have generally examined these channels separately, and the joint transmission of these channels into ASEAN agri-food commodity logistics outcomes remains largely unexamined. This study applies a Vector Autoregression (VAR) time-series modeling framework to identify and quantify the principal drivers of disruption in ASEAN agri-food logistics networks, using 4,108 daily observations spanning January 2015 to March 2026. Seven variables are jointly modeled: Baltic Dry Index daily change (D_BDI), Brent crude oil log-return (R_Brent), Geopolitical Risk Index daily change (D_GPR), Oceanic Niño Index anomaly change (D_ONI), ASEAN aggregate agricultural production return (R_ASEAN_Production), and daily price changes of Robusta and Arabica coffee. Stationarity is verified by the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests. The lag order p = 2 is selected based on BIC and HQIC. GPR shocks exert statistically significant lagged effects on Arabica price (p = 0.007) and Robusta price (p = 0.021); ONI anomaly changes significantly propagate into Robusta prices (p = 0.021). A cross-domain pathway from ONI to GPR (p = 0.010) is consistent with climate disruption signals coinciding with subsequent geopolitical risk movements. BDI first-order persistence coefficient is 0.596 (p < 0.001). Forecast Error Variance Decomposition (FEVD) shows Robusta-to-Arabica cross-variance at 44.03% at horizon 10. Durbin-Watson statistics (1.958–2.061) confirm residual white noise across all equations. These results provide quantitative inputs for engineering early-warning systems for disruption and logistics resilience planning in ASEAN agri-food supply networks.

title: Dataset Supporting a Systematic Literature Review of Climate Change Impacts on Fisheries Trade and Supply Chains
summary: Dataset Description This dataset supports the systematic literature review entitled “Impacts of Climate Change on International Trade, Competitiveness, and Supply Chains of Fisheries Commodities: A Systematic Literature Review.” The review followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting framework and used a PECOS-informed eligibility approach. Searches conducted in Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and PubMed identified 707 records. After removing 44 duplicates, 663 records were screened, seven full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and six studies were included in the final synthesis. The dataset contains structured information on study selection, study-level characteristics, climate-related stressors, fisheries trade and market outcomes, supply-chain disruptions, adaptation and resilience responses, methodological quality appraisal, and outcome-level evidence extraction. The dataset is provided to support research transparency, reproducibility, and further investigation of climate change impacts on international fisheries trade and seafood supply chains. title: Algorithmic Differential Pricing in the Digital Economy: Inherent Logic and Hierarchical Industry Regulatory Framework
summary: Digital platforms implement personalized pricing relying on massive user data and algorithm technologies, and big data driven "big data ripening" has continuously triggered consumer disputes, making algorithmic differential pricing a key challenge for digital economy governance. Taking algorithmic differential pricing as the research object, this paper draws on theories of price discrimination, behavioral pricing and regulatory economics and adopts theoretical analysis and logical deduction to explore its operational logic. Algorithmic differential pricing represents traditional price discrimination adapted to digital contexts. Supported by user data portraits, it realizes personalized "thousands of people, thousands of prices" and approximates first degree price discrimination. The outcome of algorithmic tiered pricing hinges on data advantages, user lock in and market competition, and its welfare effect is dual sided rather than simply beneficial or detrimental to markets. This paper establishes a hierarchical industry differentiated regulatory framework covering flexible supervision, stringent supervision and bottom line protection to reconcile industrial market features and consumer rights demands. It extends theoretical studies on algorithmic price discrimination and offers references for prudent regulatory practice for platform algorithmic pricing.

title: Does corporate sustainability performance mitigate the negative market reaction to the SEOs? Fresh evidence from the G-10 markets
summary: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between firms' corporate sustainability performance, reflected in their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) scores, and the market reaction to seasoned equity offerings (SEOs), in addition to examining how stock price volatility affects this relationship. Design/methodology/approach This study utilizes a sample of 2,061 different firms that conducted 4,853 SEOs over the period from 2011 to 2022 in the G-10 countries. Both the market model and the mean-adjusted models are used to analyze the market reaction to the announcement of SEOs. In addition, a series of multivariate regressions and the Heckman self-selection approach are conducted to ensure the robustness of the results. Findings The findings reveal a positive and significant impact of ESG performance on the market reaction to SEOs. Further, this positive impact is more pronounced among stocks characterized by higher stock price volatility. This confirms the critical role that corporate sustainability practices could play in conveying favorable information that helps alleviate the negative reaction in the financial markets. Practical implications From a managerial perspective, it highlights the role of the ESG discourse as a value-protection tool that firms can utilize to mitigate the negative impacts in financial markets. For policymakers, this highlights the need to ensure the quality of firms' ESG disclosures to enhance transparency in financial markets by creating stricter regulations for ESG disclosures. Originality/value To the best of our knowledge, no previous research has investigated the nexus between ESG practices, market reactions to SEOs, and stock price volatility in the context of G10 markets. Therefore, this study extends not only the literature that focuses on corporate sustainability performance, but also enriches the corporate finance literature that investigates stock price behavior and corporate actions. This study helps provide answers to a broader question: whether firms' ESG practices can indeed play a role in conveying favorable information that helps alleviate the negative reaction in the financial markets.

title: Does ESG Disclosure Reshape the Nexus Between Board Characteristics and Financial Performance? Evidence from Banks in an Emerging Economy
summary: This study investigates how board characteristics shape the financial performance of Egyptian banks. It also examines whether ESG disclosure alters the strength and direction of these relationships. Drawing on a balanced panel of the 20 largest banks operating in Egypt between 2016 and 2024, the study analyses four board attributes: board size, gender diversity, board activity, and board independence. Financial performance is captured by return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE), while ESG transparency is evaluated through a 35-item disclosure index encompassing environmental, social, governance, and economic dimensions. The empirical analysis employs bank fixed-effects models with year fixed effects and bank-clustered standard errors. Given the relatively small number of bank clusters, statistical inference is further assessed using a wild cluster bootstrap procedure with 9999 replications. The primary fixed-effects results indicate that board activity is positively and significantly associated with ROA. In contrast, board size, gender diversity, and board independence are not statistically significantly associated with ROA. For ROE, board size, gender diversity, and board activity also show no statistically significant associations. Board independence, however, is negatively associated with ROE. Overall, the findings provide limited evidence that board characteristics are systematically associated with bank financial performance, with the clearest evidence being the positive association between board activity and ROA. Moreover, the moderation analysis further shows that none of the interaction terms between ESG disclosure and the examined board characteristics is statistically significant for either ROA or ROE, providing no statistically reliable evidence that ESG disclosure moderates these relationships. By providing evidence from Egypt, an emerging economy undergoing substantial governance and sustainability reforms, this study extends the literature at the intersection of corporate governance, ESG transparency, and bank performance. It further contributes by providing empirical evidence on whether ESG disclosure operates as a boundary condition in the relationship between board governance and financial performance in the Egyptian banking sector.

title: A Study on Integration of AI with ESG Reporting
summary: Corporates operate their businesses in a very dynamic and complex landscape. The connection between corporates, society, and the eco-system is inseparable. The way of reporting business information has changed drastically due to the changing needs of information by different stakeholders and changes in reporting frameworks. BRSR aims to standardize reporting related to ESG criteria, helping stakeholders make informed decisions regarding their investments. Traditional method of reporting often requires processing huge data from different departments, which is a time-consuming process and error prone. Integration of AI in BRSR reporting can potentially lead to numerous benefits and can mitigate the challenges of various ESG reporting frameworks. This study seeks to highlight the importance of leveraging AI in ESG Reporting with an objective to exhibit the ESG Reporting preparedness of Indian Companies and the prospects and challenges of integrating AI with ESG Reporting. The study comprises secondary Data collected from Survey Reports of Deloitte and others, NSE Publications, SEBI, S&P website, etc.

title: Edible Biopolymer Coatings for Postharvest Preservation in Warm‐Chain Horticultural Supply Chain: Mechanisms, Materials, Design Strategies, and Future Directions
summary: Fresh fruit and vegetable postharvest losses reach 30%-50% between harvest and consumption, concentrated in low- and middle-income countries where warm-chain supply chains (20°C-35°C, 55%-85% relative humidity, intermittent handling) replace the refrigerated cold chains conventional technology assumes. Edible coatings from polysaccharides, proteins, and lipids offer a non-refrigeration postharvest intervention, with efficacy confirmed under controlled laboratory conditions, but commercial adoption remains marginal. This review argues that the gap between laboratory performance and field outcomes is primarily a systems-design failure, in which existing formulations optimized for stable, refrigerated conditions are not engineered to maintain function under warm-chain variability. Biopolymer materials face a three-axis trade-off, unable to simultaneously satisfy moisture barrier performance, gas exchange selectivity, and thermal-hygroscopic stability, and all three degrade predictably under warm-chain conditions through mechanisms current formulation design does not account for. Bioactive release kinetics compound this failure by depleting protection before supply chain completion, while the absence of a commodity classification framework makes the research literature noncumulative. This review makes three contributions. It provides, to the authors' knowledge, among the first integrated analyses of biopolymer coating performance failure under warm-chain conditions, distinguished by its deployment-focused approach rather than a materials-cataloging one. It formalizes this into a three-axis framework showing that composite design is physically necessary for warm-chain applications, and proposes a four-pillar warm-chain design framework comprising predictive formulation modeling, controlled-release calibration, commodity-specific coating architecture, and standardized warm-chain validation protocols. A six-phase implementation pipeline and a commodity-specific application matrix operationalize this framework into a demonstrable pathway from formulation to field deployment.

title: Selection and optimization of dual‐strategy for selling mode and preservation in e‐commerce supply chain for fresh produce
summary: Abstract Recently, e‑commerce platforms have witnessed rapid growth and successively entered the fresh produce sector. They have established deep cooperation with upstream suppliers, thereby giving rise to a variety of cooperation modes, including wholesale () or agency () modes. Besides, to guarantee the freshness of fresh produce, suppliers or platforms are required to make preservation investment, thereby giving rise to two strategies, namely, supplier‐led () or platform‐led () preservation. This paper proposes four dual strategies of , , and , and mainly explores how to select and optimize the dual‐strategy of an e‐commerce supply chain for fresh produce. The following results are found. The platform selects or () dual‐strategy when the commission rate is low or high (moderate) in most cases. However, given the sufficiently strong consumers’ freshness preference, the platform will opt for dual‑strategy even if the commission rate is relatively high. Besides, there exist three optimization types, namely, optimizing only the selling mode, only the preservation strategy, or both simultaneously. For these optimization types, the supplier can use various transfer payments to motivate the platform to adjust dual‐strategy for win–win.

title: Green Supply Chain Management and Economic Sustainability of Small and medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Enugu State, Nigeria
summary: The study evaluated the effect of green supply chain management on the economic sustainability of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Enugu State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to determine the effect of green production on cost efficiency and assess the effect of green logistics on the revenue growth of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. Primary data were collected through the administration of questionnaires. The study population comprised 3,740 staff members. A sample size of 345 was determined using Freund and William’s statistical formula. Of the questionnaires distributed, 251 were returned and correctly completed. The validity of the research instrument was assessed using content analysis, and the result was satisfactory. The reliability of the instrument was tested using the Pearson correlation coefficient (r), which yielded a reliability coefficient of 0.82, indicating good reliability. Data were presented and analysed using mean scores and standard deviations based on the four-point Likert scale. The hypotheses were tested using the Z-test statistic. The findings revealed that green production had a significant positive effect on the cost efficiency of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria (Z = 9.673, p < .05), while green logistics had a significant positive effect on the revenue growth of SMEs in the state (Z = 9.799, p < .05). The study concluded that green supply chain management plays an important role in promoting the economic sustainability of SMEs in Enugu State, Nigeria. Among other recommendations, the study recommended that SME owners and managers in Enugu State should adopt environmentally friendly production techniques, including the use of energy-efficient equipment, waste minimisation, and the efficient use of raw materials, to reduce production costs and improve cost efficiency.

title: Equilibrium Analysis of Power Structure and Farmer Risk Aversion in Green Technology Outsourcing for Agricultural Supply Chains
summary: Smallholder farmers often lack the capacity to adopt green technologies, and their risk aversion further limits green production. Outsourcing green technology to specialized service providers is a promising solution, but it remains unclear how power structure affects farmers’ adoption of such outsourcing, how supply chain members rank different power structures, and whether outsourcing always improves social welfare. To address these questions, this paper develops an equilibrium model of an agricultural supply chain consisting of a risk-averse farmer, a retailer, and a green technology service provider. The farmer may either continue traditional production or outsource green technology. Farmer risk aversion is captured by conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). We derive equilibrium decisions under three power structures: service-provider-led, retailer-led, and vertical Nash. We characterize the adoption threshold for green technology outsourcing, compare equilibrium planting acreage, green technology input, prices, and member payoffs, and evaluate social welfare. The results show that outsourcing becomes preferable when farmers are less risk averse, and the outsourcing threshold is lowest under service provider leadership. The farmer prefers vertical Nash when consumers’ green preference is low and service-provider leadership when it is high. Service providers benefit from leadership, while retailers do not always do so. Social welfare can improve under service-provider-led outsourcing but may decrease under retailer-led and vertical Nash regimes. An extension with exogenous service pricing is also analyzed. These findings provide equilibrium-based implications for sustainable agricultural outsourcing policy.

title: DEMAND-DRIVEN MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS PLANNING (DDMRP) FOR COAL INVENTORY CONTROL TO MITIGATE SUPPLY CHAIN UNCERTAINTY
summary: Abstract Upstream logistical uncertainty in the primary energy supply chain represents a critical challenge for nationally vital facilities in ensuring the continuity of electricity generation. PT XYZ faces fluctuations in barge arrivals, resulting in substantial physical coal supply deficits and declining safety stock levels. This study aims to design a proposed adaptive coal inventory control system using the Demand Driven Material Requirements Planning (DDMRP) method to mitigate supply chain uncertainty, with a focus on physical quantities (tonnage). The study employed a quantitative descriptive method with a system design approach to develop a proposed DDMRP application based on operational data from 2025. The DDMRP implementation process comprises Strategic Positioning, Buffer Profiles and Levels, Dynamic Adjustments, Demand Driven Planning, and Visual Execution. The results show that positioning the coal yard as a strategic decoupling point can serve as a separation point between external supply uncertainty and internal consumption requirements. Based on an Average Daily Usage (ADU) of 11,169 tons and a Decoupled Lead Time (DLT) of 12 days, the proposed dynamic buffer level parameters consist of a Top of Red of 42,736 tons as the minimum critical level, a Top of Yellow of 176,768 tons as the replenishment threshold, and a Top of Green of 219,503 tons as the maximum inventory level. Overall, the proposed implementation of DDMRP provides a more adaptive inventory control mechanism for responding to changes in demand and supply uncertainty, supporting material flow stability, and helping to control the risks of stockouts and excessive coal accumulation. Keywords: Supply Chain Management, Inventory Control, DDMRP, Coal, Material Flow

title: Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosure and the Financial Stability of Quoted Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: Heterogeneous Effects on Profitability, Capital, Liquidity, Asset Quality and Insolvency Risk
summary: This study examines the relationship between environmental, social and governance (ESG) disclosure and the financial stability of quoted deposit money banks in Nigeria, and whether governance structure moderates that relationship. Using panel data hand-collected from the audited annual and sustainability reports of twelve banks listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over 2015–2025, this study relates an 18-item content-analysis ESG disclosure index and its environmental, social and governance sub-indices to five bank-level stability indicators: capital adequacy, liquidity, asset quality (non-performing loans), profitability (return on assets) and insolvency risk (Z-score). Bank fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors form the baseline, and fixed-effects two-stage least squares (FE-2SLS) is used as a robustness check for potential endogeneity. The composite ESG index is positively and significantly associated with profitability, a result that persists in the FE-2SLS estimates, but its associations with liquidity, non-performing loans and the Z-score are insignificant and its association with capital adequacy is negative; the associations between disclosure and stability are therefore heterogeneous across its dimensions rather than uniformly positive. Governance structure, entered as a separate regressor, is directly associated with higher capital adequacy and profitability and with lower non-performing loans, whereas its interaction with disclosure is statistically significant only for capital adequacy and liquidity and is sensitive to the exclusion of individual banks, so that the moderation evidence is treated as fragile. Among the disclosure dimensions, governance disclosure is most consistently associated with stability, environmental disclosure is associated with lower capital adequacy and social disclosure is associated with higher non-performing loans. The near-saturation of the disclosure index among these large banks limits within-bank variation and counsels caution in interpretation. The findings suggest that regulators should prioritise the credibility and quality of disclosure, and the governance mechanisms that underpin it, rather than its quantity.

title: Digital Transformation and Sharia Human Resources Management: Challenges and Opportunities in the Industrial Era 5.0
summary: The Industrial 5.0 era demands humanistic human resource (HR) management, while the fast-growing Islamic finance industry faces the pressure of digital transformation that often exceeds the readiness of its human resources. This research aims to identify the challenges and opportunities of sharia HR management in facing digital transformation in the Industrial 5.0 era and formulate a strategic framework for its management. The research uses a qualitative approach with a case study design on Islamic banks, combining primary data from semi-structured interviews with management, questionnaires on licensed employees, and field observations, which are analyzed with the Miles and Huberman model and triangulation of sources and techniques. The results of the study show that the readiness of sharia values and ethics is high, while the readiness of digital competencies and human-technology collaboration is still lagging behind, so that the core of the problem shifts from compliance to talent development. The research concludes that sharia values, such as niyyah, amanah, itqan, and justice, function as a humanistic bridge that links technology adoption with the human-centric orientation of Industry 5.0, so that it becomes a comparative advantage, not an obstacle to modernization. The implication is that Islamic financial institutions need to shift the orientation from administrative compliance to the development of talents that are digitally competent and spiritually strong.

title: Digital transformation as a double-edged sword: boosting sales while increasing pressure on skills
summary: While the adoption of digital technology in companies has many benefits, it may also bring several challenges. Potential pressure on new skills is one of them, and it can be especially evident for SMEs. The main aim of the paper is to examine the potential consequences of digital transformation on SMEs’ sales and the availability of skills. The analysis is based on the firms’ microdata from the Flash Eurobarometer 537 (2023) questionnaire survey. The survey was conducted on more than 15000 respondent firms from 27 EU and 8 non-EU countries. The research uses a synergistic approach combining logistic regression and propensity score matching to identify the potential effects of digital technology adoption on future skill shortages and turnover. The results show that digital technology cannot close the skills gap in SMEs. Moreover, it can even further amplify the problem because it requires hiring employees with new skill sets complementary to digital technology. However, adopting digital technology can drive significant sales growth. The study presents new findings that allow us to propose recommendations for addressing skill shortages in SMEs in a rapidly changing business environment.

title: Peer-Supported Learning in the Digital Transformation of Higher Education: A Theory-Informed Systematic Review
summary: Peer support in higher education settings plays an important role in fostering collaboration, motivation, and resilience among learners in higher education. Higher education has undergone a rapid and sustained shift toward digital learning spaces, a transformation that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated and that continues to expand with the growing integration of online, hybrid, and AI-enabled learning technologies. This systematic review synthesised evidence on peer-supported learning interventions and their association with academic performance, engagement, well-being, and professional development among higher education students in online and hybrid learning environments. A comprehensive literature search of PubMed, ERIC, and Web of Science, supplemented by Google Scholar, identified 19 eligible studies published between January 2020 and December 2024, a period spanning the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath. A narrative, theory-informed synthesis was undertaken as substantial heterogeneity in study designs, interventions, and outcome measures precluded meta-analysis, and study quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Models of peer-supported learning interventions included peer-assisted learning (PAL), near-peer teaching (NPT), team-based learning (TBL), and peer-led team learning (PLTL). Structured peer-supported learning interventions were associated with improved academic performance, particularly in the development of practical and clinical skills, although the underlying evidence base is dominated by descriptive, single-group, and small-scale comparative designs rather than adequately powered controlled trials, and effect claims should be interpreted accordingly. Peer-supported learning was also associated with greater student engagement, motivation, and psychosocial well-being, including reduced anxiety and stronger connectedness in digital settings, although a minority of studies reported null or mixed results. Most studies reported feasibility and satisfaction, although effectiveness depended on structure, facilitation quality, and task complexity, and the evidence base remains disproportionately drawn from medicine and nursing disciplines. Findings were interpreted through the lenses of self-determination theory, social learning theory, and constructivist theory, suggesting that autonomy, relatedness, and active participation underpin the benefits of peer support in learning. Well-designed, structured peer-supported learning interventions show promise for enhancing both cognitive and affective outcomes in digitally mediated higher education, although confirmation across a broader range of disciplines and more rigorous comparative designs is needed.

title: Utility Billing and Debt Collection in Latvia: A Legal Audit (2026)
summary: This report presents a documentary and legal audit of residential utility billing, account migration, and extrajudicial debt collection practices in Latvia. The analysis examines two utility accounts associated with one residential apartment, including electricity consumption, historical balances, late-payment charges, and the transition of billing administration from SIA Baložu komunālā saimniecība to SIA Ķekavas nami. It also examines a debt collection notice issued by SIA PAUS KONSULTS, focusing on the transparency of debt calculations, consumer rights, evidentiary requirements, and the legal framework governing extrajudicial debt recovery. The report identifies unresolved accounting and documentation questions, including the reconciliation of historical balances, the allocation of payments, and the substantiation of collection charges. It distinguishes verified invoice arithmetic from matters requiring further documentary evidence. title: CHALLENGES OF BLENDED LEARNING AND ACCOUNTING PRACTICE IN THE BUSINESS WORLD TODAY: THE WAY FORWARD
summary: ABSTRACT: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed both educational delivery and professional accounting practice. Blended learning, which combines face-to-face instruction with online and technology-mediated learning, has increasingly become an important approach to preparing accounting students for a business environment characterized by digital accounting systems, cloud computing, data analytics, artificial intelligence, automation and other emerging technologies. Despite its potential, the implementation of blended learning in accounting education faces significant challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, unreliable electricity and internet connectivity, high technology costs, limited digital competence among lecturers and students, resistance to change, difficulties in online assessment, cybersecurity and privacy concerns, unequal access to digital devices, and weak alignment between academic training and contemporary accounting practice. These challenges can create a gap between what accounting students learn and the competencies demanded by employers. This paper examines the challenges of blended learning and accounting practice in the contemporary business world and proposes practical strategies for addressing them. The paper adopts a qualitative conceptual review approach, drawing on relevant academic and professional literature concerning blended learning, accounting education, digital transformation and professional accounting competencies. The review indicates that effective blended learning should not merely involve transferring traditional lectures to online platforms; rather, it should integrate appropriate technology, sound pedagogy, practical accounting applications, industry collaboration and continuous professional development. The paper recommends investment in digital infrastructure, regular training of accounting educators, curriculum redesign, stronger university-industry partnerships, authentic digital assessment, improved cybersecurity, access to affordable devices and internet services, and greater emphasis on data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud accounting and professional ethics. The paper concludes that a strategically designed blended learning system can help narrow the education-practice gap and produce accounting graduates capable of functioning effectively in the rapidly changing business world. title: Impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Practices on Corporate Financial Performance in the Mining Sector of Zimbabwe
summary: This study examines the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices on corporate financial performance in Zimbabwe's mining sector using a case study of Zimplats Holdings Limited. The main aim was to determine whether and to what extent ESG practices contribute to financial outcomes at the firm level. The objective of the study was to examine the overall ESG and financial performance relationship, to analyse the effects of individual ESG dimensions on financial performance, and to assess the moderating role of firm-specific factors on ESG practices. Informed by the stakeholder theory, the resource-based view, and legitimacy theory, a quantitative approach was adopted, using secondary data extracted from Zimplats' Integrated Annual Reports (2023–2025) through a structured data extraction template aligned with GRI standards. Key findings reveal a positive but lagged ESG and financial performance relationship. Governance emerged as the most stable and financially material ESG pillar, while environmental and social investments showed transitional efficiency deterioration before expected long-term gains. Firm-specific factors such as asset expansion, capital structure, production volume, and multinational ownership, significantly moderated the timing and magnitude of financial returns, compressing short-term profitability indicators such as return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE). The study contributes firm-level empirical evidence on unlisted Zimbabwean mining firms, extending ESG theory to emerging market contexts. Recommendations include targeting governance enhancements for immediate financial returns, allowing longer investment horizons for environmental and social initiatives, and maintaining conservative capital structures to sustain ESG investment during earnings volatility.

title: From Consumption To Investment: Defense Spending and Strategic Industrial Development In Indonesia
summary: Indonesia’s defense budget has increased substantially, yet spending remains dominated by routine operational and management needs rather than productive investment. This study analyzes the transformation of Indonesia’s defense spending into strategic investment through a “spend-to-invest” approach in support of the Asta Cita national development agenda. Using a descriptive qualitative design and document analysis of defense spending data from 2021 to 2025, the study finds that the defense budget rose from Rp154.88 trillion in 2021 to Rp264.35 trillion in 2025, but the spending structure remains oriented toward management support and operational needs. Investment in research and development, local content (TKDN), technology mastery, and domestic defense industry involvement remains limited. Key obstacles include routine spending dominance, import-dependent procurement, weak technology transfer, and reliance on foreign components. The study recommends a five-pillar “spend-to-invest” model: budget recomposition, local-content-based procurement, research and technology transfer, domestic supply chain resilience, and indicator-based governance. This model can strengthen industrial self-reliance and economic resilience in support of Indonesia Emas 2045.

title: Perceived Green Innovation Ambidexterity as a Strategic Signal in By‐Product Recycling: Employee Green Behavior, Environmental Consciousness, and Job Satisfaction
summary: ABSTRACT In by‐product recycling businesses, pursuing green innovation ambidexterity is important, but its benefits depend on how employees enact this strategic orientation. Drawing on signaling theory, we conducted two studies to examine how perceived green innovation ambidexterity is related to employee green behavior and job satisfaction, and investigate the role of individual environmental consciousness in these relationships. For Study 1, we used survey data from 308 by‐product recycling workers in six countries and found that employee green behavior mediated the relationship between perceived green innovation ambidexterity and job satisfaction. Individual environmental consciousness strengthened the effect of perceived green innovation ambidexterity and employee green behavior on job satisfaction. For Study 2, we conducted a scenario‐based experiment with 204 participants, providing supplementary evidence in an experimental setting. Overall, we show how employees interpret green innovation ambidexterity as a strategic signal and translate it into green behavior and job satisfaction, with responses varying according to environmental consciousness.

title: Sustainable Finance dan Green Investment: Transformasi Keuangan Berkelanjutan dalam Mewujudkan Climate Resilience di Indonesia
summary: Perubahan iklim telah berkembang menjadi risiko multidimensional yang memengaruhi lingkungan, perekonomian, pembangunan, dan stabilitas sistem keuangan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis perkembangan sustainable finance, peran green investment, serta kontribusinya terhadap ketahanan iklim di Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan studi pustaka dan data sekunder dari OJK, Kementerian Keuangan, Bank Dunia, ADB, Bappenas, serta artikel ilmiah yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan perkembangan sustainable finance melalui penguatan regulasi, TKBI, dan instrumen obligasi serta sukuk berkelanjutan. Green investment berkembang melalui pembiayaan hijau dan Green Sukuk, tetapi kebutuhan pembiayaan iklim masih jauh lebih besar dibandingkan kapasitas yang tersedia.

title: Economic Feasibility & Carbon Emission Reduction of EV Haul Truck Implementation: A Case Study of Pongkeru Nickel Mining Concession
summary: Background: Indonesia's nickel mining supports the global EV battery supply chain but relies on diesel haul trucks, causing high fuel consumption, emissions, and exposure to fuel-price volatility. Electrifying hauling can improve efficiency, reduce direct emissions, and strengthen resilience to energy-price and transition risks. Objective: This study analyzes the economic feasibility, environmental impact, and energy-efficiency gains of replacing diesel haul trucks with EV hauling at the Pongkeru Block nickel mine, Indonesia. Methods: A Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) approach using Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and Payback Period (PBP) was applied under Conservative, Base Case, and Optimistic scenarios. The scenarios were combined into a probability-weighted expected NPV. The analysis was complemented by activity-based carbon accounting, ESG-integrated valuation with carbon-price scenarios, energy-efficiency analysis, and one-way sensitivity analysis. Results: EV hauling yields NPVs of USD 87.85, 116.99, and 138.70 million under the Conservative, Base Case, and Optimistic scenarios, respectively, versus USD 25.15, 52.57, and 85.18 million for diesel. The expected NPV is USD 112.59 million for EV versus USD 50.86 million for diesel. EV payback is two to three years versus three to five years for diesel. Direct diesel-related emissions are estimated at 142,697.48 tCO₂e over the mine life. EV hauling shows 2.1–3.2 times higher energy-conversion efficiency and 49%–65% lower input-energy requirements. Conclusion: EV-based hauling is economically favorable across all scenarios and delivers substantial environmental and energy-efficiency benefits. Its long-term value depends on reliable electricity supply, adequate charging infrastructure, lower-carbon power sources, effective transition-risk management, and access to sustainable financing.

title: The Influence of Institutional Ownership, Managerial Ownership, Independent Board of Commissioners, Audit Comittee on Company Values (Study of Banking Companies Listed On The IDX For The 2020-2023 Period)
summary: Abstract: Good Corporate Governance (GCG) plays a crucial role in determining a company's value, with factors such as institutional and managerial ownership, the independent board of commissioners, and the audit committee significantly influencing investor decisions. In the banking sector, fluctuations in income, asset ratios, and equity ratios can impact investor confidence and decision-making. This study aims to examine the influence of institutional ownership, managerial ownership, the independent board of commissioners, and the audit committee on company value. Using a quantitative associative approach, the research analyzes a sample of 88 companies selected through purposive sampling, a non-probability sampling method. Data were collected from the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) and official company websites, and analyzed using SPSS Version 26. The results of the findings showed that: (H1) accepted; (H2) rejected; (H3) rejected; (H4) accepted; (H5) accepted. The results imply that governance mechanisms should be considered separately, as audit committee effectiveness and institutional ownership, and non-significant associations need not be interpreted as uniform governance effects.

title: Assessing the impact of digital transformation on healthcare performance: A case study of healthcare establishments in the province of Midelt
summary: In Morocco, digitalization now stands among the primary levers for modernizing the healthcare sector, and a national programme supports the digital overhaul of care delivery and of the establishments providing it. Whether such change translates into better performance remains an open empirical question. The present study puts that question to the test in the province of Midelt, a mountainous territory characterised by a dispersed population and by highly uneven access to services. A structured questionnaire was administered to 103 healthcare professionals who mobilise digital tools in their daily work, and perceived performance was measured through four dimensions drawn from the literature, namely efficiency, quality of care, accessibility and equity of services. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and multiple linear regression were computed with IBM SPSS Statistics (v.26). The model explains 60.4% of the variance in perceived performance. Two predictors reach significance, service efficiency (β = 0.371, p < 0.001) and quality of care (β = 0.342, p < 0.001), which supports H1 and H2. Accessibility (p = 0.273) and equity (p = 0.127) remain below the significance threshold, an outcome traced to local constraints, starting with a telemedicine programme still confined to the pilot stage. The findings plead for patient-centred digital solutions, sustained investment in suitable tools and continuous strengthening of the digital skills of healthcare personnel.

title: Heavy Metal Contamination of Wetland Soil and Water in the Jama'are River Basin, Nigeria: Implications for Livelihoods and Environmental Governance
summary: Abstract The Jama'are River wetland in the Hadejia – Jama'are floodplain, northern Nigeria, is utilized for farming, fishing, and grazing by the riverine communities, but there is little information regarding the contamination of the wetland with metals. The study was conducted in the 2026 rainy season where the topsoils and surface water were sampled from three stations beside the maize farmland, sugarcane farmland and the waste dumping site, and analyzed with atomic absorption spectrophotometry to determine the levels of cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), lead (Pb) and zinc (Zn). Zn and Pb dominated in both media (soil Zn 87.30 and Pb 40.60 mg/kg; water Pb 0.366 and Zn 0.280 mg/L). A guideline-normalized Pollution Load Index (PLI) was less than one for soil (0.133–0.224) and water (0.152–0.299), and soil metals were not greater than benchmarks. Water Cd was however 1.8–2.3 times higher than the limit set by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for irrigation water; Cd and Pb were 3.6–4.6 and 20.7–28.2 times higher than the Nigerian regulatory reference values, respectively; and there was a significant enrichment of Cd in soils because of the comparison of average shale values. The low composite index thus obscured risks pertinent to irrigation farmers and water users. The results suggest that regular monitoring of Cd and Pb concentrations, rein in open dumping and agrochemicals use, and community understanding of water quality in irrigation water be implemented. title: Critical Success Factors for AI Training Robot Adoption in Accounting SMEs: An Integrated Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP Approach
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) are transforming accounting services toward intelligent, data-driven professional services. However, small and medium-sized accounting firms (SMEs) face barriers to AI adoption, including limited resources, technological capabilities, employee skills, and regulatory uncertainty. This study identifies and prioritizes the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing AI training robot adoption in Taiwanese accounting SMEs. The framework integrates the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, Task–Technology Fit (TTF), Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Human–Computer Trust (HCT), and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). We used a two-round Delphi process with 15 experts to refine the CSFs, followed by DEMATEL to identify causal relationships and ANP to assess their relative priorities. The DEMATEL results indicate that the Technological dimension is the strongest causal driver (D−R = 1.355), followed by the Organizational dimension (D−R = 0.435), whereas Decision Making is the principal effect dimension (D−R = −1.781). The findings further emphasize task–technology alignment, AI maturity, regulatory conditions, top management support, employee AI competence, and human–computer trust. Overall, AI adoption represents an integrated organizational transformation rather than merely a technological investment. The proposed Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP framework provides systematic decision support for resource prioritization, organizational readiness, capability development, and sustainable AI-enabled digital transformation in accounting SMEs. title: Harnessing Untapped Indigenous African Philosophies to Address Contemporary Supply Chain Management Challenges: Insights from Òwè and Àáró
summary: This article examines how the Yoruba concepts of ọ̀wẹ̀ and àáró can be integrated into modern supply chain management (SCM) to address persistent problems of inequality, inefficiency, and systemic fragility. Drawing on indigenous West African practice, it shows how ọ̀wẹ̀, a model of altruistic collaboration, and àáró, a structured system of reciprocal labor exchange, can foster fairness, trust, and resilience. The paper combines this indigenous knowledge with established SCM theories to build an integrated framework for contemporary SCM challenges. We argue that ọ̀wẹ̀ supports weaker actors and encourages inclusivity, while àáró improves efficiency through organized reciprocity. The two offer concrete strategies for managing disruptions and reducing resource dependence. A conceptual matrix links these practices to current supply chain issues, highlighting their potential to improve resource sharing, stakeholder collaboration, and network stability. The article also proposes research questions and methodologies for empirical testing to advance sustainable SCM practice. More broadly, it extends theoretical understanding of collaborative supply chain models and offers practical insight for building more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable global supply chains.

title: Digital Economy and Economic Growth: Productivity Channels, Global Evidence, and Policy Priorities for an Inclusive Digital Transition
summary: The digital economy has become a central component of contemporary economic transformation, but its contribution to growth is neither automatic nor evenly distributed. This article examines the principal channels through which digitalization can influence economic growth and synthesizes recent global evidence on productivity, innovation, employment, human capital, infrastructure, and institutional readiness. The study adopts a structured narrative-review approach drawing on established economic literature, recent peer-reviewed studies, and international policy reports. Three research questions guide the analysis: through which mechanisms does digitalization affect economic growth; why do growth effects differ across countries, firms, and sectors; and which policy conditions are most important for converting digital adoption into inclusive and sustainable economic gains? The review finds that digital technologies can raise productivity by lowering transaction and coordination costs, improving information use, enabling automation, expanding market access, and accelerating innovation. However, recent evidence also shows that productivity effects may be heterogeneous and nonlinear, particularly where firms lack complementary organizational capabilities, skills, finance, or absorptive capacity. Digital infrastructure and broadband remain foundational, while human capital and digital skills determine the extent to which firms and workers can exploit technological opportunities. Artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, and digital platforms are likely to strengthen these channels but may also intensify labor-market adjustment, market concentration, cybersecurity risks, and digital inequality. The article proposes an integrated policy framework centered on infrastructure, diffusion, skills, innovation capacity, institutional quality, and inclusion. It concludes that digitalization should be understood as a complementary-capabilities process rather than a stand-alone technological shock: long-term growth depends on how effectively digital technologies are combined with human capital, organizational change, competition, and responsive public policy.

title: The Effect of Stakeholder Pressure on Environmental Audit Quality: The Moderating Role of Sustainability-Oriented Organizational Culture in Firms Listed on the Hanoi Stock Exchange
summary: Amid growing pressure from stakeholders on Vietnamese listed firms to disclose environmental information, and as firms listed on the Hanoi Stock Exchange enter a critical phase of market restructuring, this study aims to clarify the mechanism through which stakeholder pressure affects environmental audit quality, while elucidating the moderating role of sustainability oriented organizational culture in this relationship. Using a desk-research method that synthesizes, analyzes, evaluates and compares domestic and international secondary literature, the study develops an analytical framework integrating stakeholder theory and institutional theory. The synthesized results show that coercive pressure from state regulatory agencies currently dominates the environmental disclosure behavior of this group of firms, while market-based pressure from investors and customers remains relatively weak; sustainability-oriented organizational culture is found to amplify the effect of stakeholder pressure, although the degree of moderation is uneven, being more limited for administrative pressure than for market-based pressure. On this basis, the study contributes an integrated theoretical framework and proposes practical implications for regulators, listed firms and auditors during the restructuring of Vietnam's stock market.

title: From Stakeholder Pressure to Public Value: The Role of Non‐Financial Reporting in the Waste Management Sector
summary: ABSTRACT The research investigates the creation and destruction of public value in the Italian waste management sector through stakeholder engagement and the quality of nonfinancial reporting (NFR). Drawing on stakeholder theory and public service logic, public value is conceptualized as the result of dynamic relational processes, where stakeholder salience mediates the impact of external pressure on organizational priorities. A structural model is developed and empirically tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) on a sample of 69 Italian waste management firms disclosing nonfinancial information. The analysis shows that stakeholder pressure (especially from customers and governments) affects the quality and inclusiveness of NFR. High‐quality NFR enhances stakeholder salience by absorbing environmental and social claims into governance and reporting practices, promoting a more responsive and accountable service delivery. Public value is measured by using a hybrid set of indicators combining financial performance (ROI and ROE) with socio‐environmental outcomes (e.g., recycling rates and waste reduction). The findings highlight the strategic importance of participatory, materiality‐driven reporting in fostering public value creation.

title: Implementation of the Indonesian Sustainable Finance Taxonomy as an Instrument for Renewable Energy Transition Based on Sustainable Business Strategy and Practices in the Banking Sector
summary: In response to climate change and Indonesia’s commitment to achieving Net Zero Emissions by 2060, sustainable finance has become an essential instrument for supporting the energy transition. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) introduced the Indonesian Sustainable Finance Taxonomy (TKBI) to classify economic activities into green and transition categories, providing guidance for financial institutions in allocating sustainable financing. However, the continued involvement of banks in syndicated lending to coal-related corporations raises concerns about the effectiveness of sustainable finance implementation. This study examines the implementation of the TKBI in encouraging financial institutions and corporations to support renewable energy financing and evaluates the role of the banking sector in facilitating Indonesia’s energy transition. Employing a normative juridical approach with a descriptive analytical method, the research analyzes primary, secondary, and tertiary legal materials, supported by relevant policy and regulatory documents. The findings indicate that the TKBI serves as a strategic regulatory framework for directing financial institutions and corporations toward a just and sustainable energy transition. It provides a classification mechanism that encourages banks to integrate environmental, social, and governance considerations into financing decisions, business policies, and risk management strategies. Nevertheless, continued financing of coal-related activities highlights challenges in aligning banking practices with national sustainability objectives. The study concludes that strengthening regulatory implementation, institutional accountability, and sustainable financing practices is essential to enhancing the banking sector’s contribution to renewable energy development and achieving Indonesia’s Net Zero Emissions target by 2060.

title: Analysis of PT Allo Bank Indonesia’s Financial Soundness Using the RGEC Method: A Case Study of 2019–2024
summary: The digital transformation of banking has increased the importance of assessing bank soundness, particularly among digital banks. This study evaluates PT Allo Bank Indonesia Tbk during 2019–2024 using the Risk Profile, Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Earnings, and Capital (RGEC) framework. A descriptive quantitative approach was applied using secondary data from annual reports. Six indicators were examined: Non-Performing Loan (NPL), Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), GCG rating, Return on Assets (ROA), Net Interest Margin (NIM), and Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR). NPL declined from 10.16% in 2019 to below 1% during 2021–2024, while LDR peaked at 163.19% in 2022. GCG improved from a rating of 3 to 2, and ROA and CAR strengthened. The composite score rose from 66.67% in 2019 to 86.67% in 2021, then stabilized at 83.33% during 2022–2024. The average was 80.00%, indicating improved bank soundness, although liquidity risk remained a concern.

title: When Governance Meets Artificial Intelligence: AI-Enabled Industrial Robotics, Environmental Governance, and Carbon Emissions in context of Chinese provinces
summary: China’s decarbonization puzzle is stark: energy-related CO₂ emissions climbed to about 12.6 Gt in 2023—roughly one-third of the global total—even as industrial automation surged, with 276,288 robots installed that year, the most worldwide. In parallel, environmental governance has been emerged as the key factor to influence the carbon emissions in China. These cross-currents motivate our central question: how do industrial robotic penetration (RBT) and governance efforts, separately and jointly, influence China’s provincial carbon trajectories? Using panel data for 30 provinces (2007–2022), we conduct pre-diagnostics for cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, and serial correlation, then estimate Feasible GLS models as main estimation approach. The baseline results show that higher RBT is associated with lower emissions, consistent with process upgrading and energy-efficient production. By contrast, environmental governance correlates positively with emissions in linear specifications, indicating that governance metrics often scale with high-pressure contexts. The interaction term of industrial robotic penetration and environmental governance is positive, suggesting that governance attention increases where automation uptake is already responding to tougher environmental conditions. Robustness using Prais–Winsten confirms the signs and significance. Heterogeneity analysis reveals a stronger abatement effect of RBT in western regions—where scale effects are smaller and upgrading is earlier—and a weaker effect in the combined central–eastern group with dense industrial ecosystems. Policy implications are threefold: prioritize automation-led efficiency where marginal gains are largest; align governance with technology adoption and energy management rather than inputs alone; and differentiate regional pathways to synchronize industrial upgrading with decarbonization.

title: PoFi: Pocket Finance — Automated Behavioral Fintech Ecosystem Concept & Specification
summary: This document provides the complete intellectual property specification, problem analysis, architectural framework, and mitigation strategies for "PoFi" (Pocket Finance)—an automated behavioral fintech ecosystem tailored for Malaysian university students and youths. Grounded in behavioral economics (Richard Thaler's Nudge Theory and Daniel Kahneman’s System 1/2 thinking) and addressing the local youth debt crisis documented by AKPK, PoFi integrates secure Open Finance aggregation (OmniSync), virtual bill ringfencing (Auto-Vault), and a Behavioral Spending Pattern AI featuring an Overspend-to-Save retroactive micro-penalty savings loop.

title: AN APRIASAL OF PIERCING THE CORPORATE VEIL DOCTRINE UNDER THE ETHIOPIAN CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REGIME: PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE NEW COMMERCIAL CODE OF ETHIOPIA AND BANKING BUSINESS LAWS
summary: Modern company law is founded on two key principles: separate legal personality and limited liability. A company is recognized as a distinct legal entity from its shareholders, enabling it to own property, enter contracts, and sue or be sued in its own name. Shareholders are generally liable only to the extent of their share capital. This protection, known as the corporate veil, encourages business activity by shielding shareholders from personal liability for corporate debts. However, limited liability is not absolute. When the corporate form is abused for unlawful or fraudulent purposes, courts may disregard the company’s separate legal personality and hold shareholders, directors, or managers personally liable. This process is known as piercing or lifting the corporate veil. The 2021 Ethiopian Commercial Code introduced significant reforms to corporate law by expanding the grounds for piercing the corporate veil and incorporating the business judgment rule. These reforms promote professional management, enhance accountability, and protect directors from liability for honest decisions made in good faith and in the company’s best interests. Using a doctrinal and qualitative research approach, this study examines the newly introduced grounds for corporate veil piercing and their underlying rationale.

title: DIGITAL TWIN AND IOT-ENABLED PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE MARKETING: A USAGE-COUPLED CONFORMAL REPLENISHMENT FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING B2B CUSTOMER LOYALTY IN AVIATION SUPPLY CHAINS
summary: Maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) customers judge an aviation supplier on one outcome: whether the part is on the shelf when the aircraft needs it. It suggests a predictive-maintenance-coupled digital-twin framework, PDT-LOY, which combines usage-driven demand learning, distribution-free protection against stockouts, a replay digital twin, and an asymmetric trust-state proxy for B2B loyalty. It is evaluated on a public synthetic dataset containing 180 part–location series over 72 months (12,960 records), which is trained on a subset of 2018–2021 and calibrated on 2022 and tested out of sample on 2023. The usage-coupled variant of the gradient-boosting demand learner (GBC) further improves the mean absolute error by 6.9% over the 12-month moving average; the impact of the usage signal on the mean absolute error is small (−1.0%), but not significant at 5% (p = 0.052). The realised coverage is 0.965 for Mondrian conformal upper bounds at the 0.95 target, as compared to 0.912 for Gaussian safety stock. The proposed policy boosts the fill rate from 73.9% (observed legacy record) to 97.0%, requiring only 2.0 fewer inventory units and 2.2% fewer units of inventory than Gaussian safety stock at a 95% fill rate. The loyalty-at-risk proxy drops to 6.6 per cent of series-months from 24.7 per cent. The machine learning approach provides little additional benefit above days-of-cover stockout early-warning, with a high AUC of 0.987 for stock cover. Results are simulation-based & with a proxy for loyalty.

title: Nursing-Led Digital Transformation: A Qualitative Exploration of Nurses’ Experiences Implementing Information and Communication Technologies Across Professional Areas
summary: This qualitative descriptive study explores the experiences and perspectives of nurses in Spain regarding the implementation of information and communication technologies (ICT) across different professional settings. Based on semi-structured interviews with 21 nurses from diverse roles, thematic analysis reveals an ambivalent view. On one hand, ICT is seen as a tool to improve efficiency, quality of care, professional visibility, and nursing leadership, with potential to humanise care. On the other hand, significant barriers persist. Organisational challenges include limited resources, insufficient institutional support, unequal access to training, and bureaucratic constraints. At the individual level, resistance to change, generational digital divides, fear of technological replacement, and lack of training are key obstacles. Social media is perceived as useful but raises ethical concerns related to privacy and professionalism. Participants emphasise the need for continuous, accessible training, equitable institutional support, and active nurse involvement in the design of digital tools. Overall, effective ICT implementation requires strong nursing leadership and integrative strategies.

title: Building Resilient SACCOs for the Future: A Global Bibliometric Analysis of Financial Sustainability, Governance, Digital Transformation, and Emerging Research Frontiers
summary: Purpose: This paper provides a comprehensive examination of the intellectual framework, publication output, conceptual context, and thematic development in the field of cooperative sustainability studies, focusing specifically on savings and credit cooperatives (SACCOs). Method: A bibliometric analysis was carried out over 2007-2026, using 4,399 articles published in 1,781 journals from Scopus database. Biblioshiny/Bibliometrix and VOSviewer software have been used for analysis of these articles, including performance metrics, co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, thematic mapping and thematic development. Results: The development of this field of research has been stable and the average annual growth rate makes up 11.94%, while 25.21% of the research is done collaboratively. The journal Sustainability (Switzerland) has the greatest number of publications, while the most cited author is E Ostrom. The co-citation structure is significantly formed by the book Governing the Commons and emphasizes the significance of ideas behind collective action and institutional governance. Sustainable development has been chosen as the focal thematic area and it has links to cooperatives as well as to human dimensions, decision making, resilience, adaptation, governance and leadership. Contribution: Based on the findings from this study, a Five-Phase Framework for Sustainable and Resilient SACCOs is proposed, which involves the integration of strategic sustainability conceptualization, evidence synthesis, multidimensional assessment, governance and resilience, as well as continuous adaptive learning in the sustainable and resilient cooperative organizations.

title: The mediating role of artificial intelligence perception and creative idea generation in the impact of sustainable leadership on digital transformation and circular economy awareness
summary: Introduction Today, sustainable leadership is a strategic leadership approach that addresses environmental, social, and economic priorities from a holistic perspective while at the same time driving digital transformation processes. The research aims to explain how sustainable leaders mobilize organizational resources, technological infrastructure, and human creativity within the framework of Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Methods The research was conducted on 456 white-collar employees working in small and medium-sized enterprises operating in Giresun, Kars, and Kırşehir provinces. The data collected by the convenience sampling method were analyzed using the PLS-SEM method with the SmartPLS 4.1.1 program. Results The analysis results show that sustainable leadership has significant and positive effects on perceptions of artificial intelligence, the generation of creative ideas, digital transformation, and awareness of the circular economy. It was found that the perception of artificial intelligence (AI) has a significant effect on both digital transformation and awareness of the circular economy. It was also determined that creative idea generation has significant effects on digital transformation and awareness of the circular economy. The results of the mediation analyses revealed a partial mediating role for all variables. Discussion The findings reveal that sustainable leadership is not limited to the environmental and social responsibility dimension and is a strategic element that directs digital transformation processes, shapes perceptions towards artificial intelligence, and encourages organizational creativity.

title: SANOAT KORXONALARIGA XORIJIY INVESTITSIYALARNI JALB QILISHDA ESG STANDARTLARINING ROLI

title: Bridging Green Supply Chain Management Barriers With Industry 4.0 Solutions in the Textile Industry: An Integrated Multicriteria Decision‐Making Framework for Sustainable Manufacturing
summary: ABSTRACT The textile and apparel industry is among the most environmentally intensive industrial sectors, making the adoption of green supply chain management (GSCM) essential for achieving sustainable production, but the implementation of these management practices in emerging economies is hindered by multiple organizational, technological, and economic barriers. However, Industry 4.0 technologies offer significant opportunities to enhance sustainability and operational efficiency across supply chains. This study investigates the major barriers to GSCM implementation in the textile and apparel industry of Bangladesh and evaluates the effectiveness of Industry 4.0 tools in overcoming these barriers. An integrated multicriteria decision‐making framework combining ISM, MICMAC analysis, VIKOR, and TOPSIS was employed. Twelve barriers were identified through literature review and expert consultation. ISM–MICMAC analysis revealed that lack of top management commitment was the most influential driving barrier with high driving power and low dependence. The identified influential barriers were subsequently used as evaluation criteria for assessing the effectiveness of seven Industry 4.0 technologies. VIKOR results indicated that Internet of Things (IoT) and big data and artificial intelligence provided the most effective compromise solutions for mitigating GSCM barriers, while TOPSIS ranked big data and artificial intelligence as the best‐performing technology followed closely by IoT. The findings demonstrate that data‐centric and real‐time monitoring technologies possess strong potential to improve traceability, decision‐making, communication, and sustainability performance within textile supply chains. This study contributes to the GSCM literature by integrating causal barrier analysis with Industry 4.0 technology prioritization and provides practical insights for policymakers and textile manufacturers seeking sustainable industrial transformation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Finance and Accounting: A Critical Review of Applications, Transformative Impact, Challenges and Future Research Directions
summary: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is progressively reshaping the conceptual and operational foundations of finance and accounting. What began primarily as the automation of routine and rule-based processes has evolved into the application of machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics and intelligent automation to increasingly complex financial and accounting decisions. Against this background, the present paper critically reviews the literature on the impact of AI on finance and accounting, with particular attention to financial forecasting, bankruptcy prediction, financial statement analysis, auditing, fraud detection, credit-risk assessment, investment analysis, organizational performance and professional transformation. The review demonstrates that AI has considerable potential to enhance computational efficiency, predictive capability, anomaly detection and decision support. However, the literature does not establish technological superiority as an automatic consequence of AI adoption. Rather, the effectiveness of AI is contingent upon data quality, model selection, organizational readiness, employee competencies, governance arrangements and the ability of professionals to interpret algorithmic outputs. An important theme emerging from the literature is the transition of accounting and finance from predominantly retrospective and transaction-oriented functions toward more predictive, analytical and strategically embedded roles. At the same time, increased reliance on algorithmic decision-making introduces concerns relating to explainability, bias, data privacy, cybersecurity, professional accountability and regulatory oversight. The review therefore argues that the long-term significance of AI lies less in the replacement of finance and accounting professionals than in the reconfiguration of professional work through human-AI complementarity. The paper concludes by identifying gaps concerning implementation, longitudinal organizational outcomes, explainable AI, professional competencies and emerging-economy contexts, thereby providing directions for future research. title: Not a silver bullet: a systematic review of Fintech’s role in bank liquidity creation
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how FinTech adoption reshapes bank liquidity creation under digital financial transformation. It identifies the mechanisms linking FinTech to liquidity outcomes and the key limitations that keep the FinTech–liquidity literature fragmented. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted using the PRISMA framework and Scopus database up to 2025. From 5,313 initial records, 22 empirical articles were retained after screening and eligibility assessment and analyzed through structured coding and descriptive bibliographic mapping using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Findings The review identifies four mechanisms linking FinTech to bank liquidity creation: information enhancement, process efficiency and funding reconfiguration, risk moderation and liquidity hoarding, and competition-driven market restructuring. FinTech does not exert a uniform effect on liquidity creation; its effects are contingent, mechanism-dependent, and institutionally mediated. It may increase, reduce, or redistribute liquidity creation across different market and regulatory conditions. The literature remains geographically concentrated, relies on heterogeneous proxy-based FinTech measures, and shows uneven causal identification. Research limitations/implications The study calls for theories that conceptualize FinTech as a strategic capability and better account for institutional conditions, competition, regulation, and bank-level capabilities. Practical implications The findings help banks align digital strategies with liquidity management and risk governance, while guiding regulators to balance digital financial innovation with financial stability. Originality/value This review offers an article-level mechanism synthesis that explains why FinTech may increase, reduce or redistribute bank liquidity creation. It also positions FinTech-enabled liquidity creation within innovation-science debates and develops a focused agenda for future research.

title: Artificial Intelligence Transformation in Modern Banking Ecosystems: Structural, Operational, and Governance Challenges
summary: The objective of this study is to investigate the comprehensive integration of artificial intelligence within modern banking and financial ecosystems by analysing its profound structural, operational, and macroeconomic implications. Drawing on recent empirical literature and institutional data, the work examines how AI technologies—ranging from machine learning algorithms to agentic workflows and specialised small models—are transforming retail banking, risk management, credit scoring, and regulatory compliance. The research shows that while AI adoption significantly improves operational efficiency, default prediction accuracy, and customer personalisation, it also introduces complex governance challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy vulnerabilities, and shifts in profit pools. The analysis also evaluates AI’s dual role in fostering sustainable green finance and corporate ESG integration, alongside its paradoxical capacity to influence shadow banking dynamics. By proposing an integrated technological and governance framework featuring zero-trust architecture and explainable artificial intelligence, this study outlines a strategic roadmap for financial institutions transitioning toward resilient, secure, and highly automated digital ecosystems.
