title: IMPROVING THE INVESTMENT STRATEGY FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISES
summary: This study examines approaches to improving the investment strategies of industrial enterprises in Uzbekistan to ensure that the recent expansion of investment contributes to sustainable industrial development. Drawing on official statistical data for 2021–2025 from the National Statistics Committee and the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, the research employs structural, comparative, and concentration analyses, including concentration ratios, the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI), the regional maximum-to-minimum ratio, and the coefficient of variation, complemented by a SWOT analysis. Fixed capital investment increased from 236.6 trillion soums in 2021 to 591.1 trillion soums in 2025, representing approximately 1.8-fold growth in real terms. Utilised foreign investment and loans reached USD 43.1 billion in 2025, including USD 38.2 billion in foreign direct investment. Foreign sources accounted for 71.4% of fixed capital investment, while two partner countries represented 43% of total foreign investment. Furthermore, the region receiving the highest investment volume attracted 6.1 times as much investment as the region receiving the lowest volume, highlighting opportunities to improve the geographical distribution of investment. Green finance is at an emerging stage of development, offering further opportunities to integrate sustainability principles into industrial investment strategies. Based on these findings, the study proposes a five-component framework encompassing the diversification of investment sources, the introduction of green and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) financing instruments, the development of public–private partnerships and industrial clusters, the implementation of risk-sharing mechanisms, and the establishment of a key performance indicator (KPI)-based monitoring system with measurable baseline indicators.

title: Does talking more but doing less in digital transformation affect total factor productivity? Evidence from large language models
summary: Amid the rapid expansion of digital transformation, understanding the economic consequences of corporate digital catering has become increasingly important. Combining large language model-based textual analysis with financial data, this paper constructs a measure of corporate digital catering and examines its association with firm productivity. Using Chinese A-share listed firms, we find a negative association between digital catering and total factor productivity, a pattern that is generally supported by alternative specifications and measurement checks. Further analysis provides supportive evidence consistent with two potential channels: higher operating burdens and tighter financing constraints. The negative association is more pronounced among firms with higher information asymmetry, weaker external governance, and greater digital transformation difficulty, and in regions with weaker market competition, poorer government–market relations, and less developed digital infrastructure. These findings provide new evidence on the authenticity and economic consequences of digital transformation.

title: The Impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure and Mining Commodity Price Volatility on Stock Returns for Mining Sector Companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2019–2023)
summary: This study examines the impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Disclosure and commodity price volatility on the stock returns of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2019–2023 period. Based on signaling theory, In resource-intensive industries, ESG disclosure serves as a non-financial signal that lessens information asymmetry and directs investment choices. Indonesian mining companies face pressure from regulators and investors for comprehensive sustainability reporting, yet much of the disclosure remains symbolic amid fluctuations in global commodity markets such as coal, gold, and nickel. Previous studies have shown mixed results regarding the impact of ESG, while commodity volatility adds external uncertainty to stock performance. This study addresses these gaps by investigating: (1) whether ESG disclosures significantly affect stock returns, and (2) the role of commodity price volatility in this relationship. Using a quantitative method via multiple linear regression on 26 companies (130 firm-year observations), ESG is measured using Refinitiv scores and volatility using monthly price standard deviations. These findings aim to provide insights for investors and managers regarding sustainability signals in emerging markets.

title: Long-term asset valuation and accounting in Uzbekistan: a comparative analysis of national accounting standards
summary: Ushbu maqolada aksiyadorlik jamiyatlarida uzoq muddatli aktivlarni baholash va ular hisobini yuritishning milliy me'yoriy-uslubiy tamoyillari tadqiq etiladi. Hujjatli, tarixiy va qiyosiy-uslubiy tahlil orqali asosiy vositalar va nomoddiy aktivlarni tan olish, boshlang'ich qiymatni shakllantirish, keyingi baholash, qayta baholash, amortizatsiya va hisob siyosati o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik aniqlanadi. Maqola nazariy-me'yoriy tahlilga asoslangan bo'lib, empirik samaradorlik haqidagi da'volarni ilgari surmaydi.

title: ESG Performance and Cross-Border M&A Entry: The Innovation Capability Channel and the Moderating Role of Ownership Concentration
summary: This study examines whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance affects Chinese firms’ choice of cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&As) as a mode of foreign-market entry. Drawing on stakeholder theory, the resource-based view, and the capability perspective, we argue that stronger ESG performance can reduce a firm’s reliance on acquiring an incumbent platform abroad by strengthening internally accumulated capabilities. We examine innovation capability as a mechanism through which ESG performance may influence entry-mode choice and ownership concentration as a governance condition that shapes the strength of this relationship. Using 17,395 firm-year observations of Chinese listed firms between 2010 and 2024, we combine Huazheng ESG ratings with information on overseas investment, firm characteristics, patents, and ownership structure. The baseline results show that ESG performance is negatively associated with the likelihood of cross-border M&A entry in the subsequent year. Economically, a one-standard-deviation increase in log ESG is associated with a 0.725 percentage-point decline in the probability of acquisition-based entry, equivalent to approximately 3.68% of the sample mean, calculated from the displayed estimates. Additional evidence shows that ESG performance is positively associated with subsequent patent-based innovation capability, providing evidence consistent with the proposed innovation capability mechanism. Moreover, ownership concentration strengthens the negative association between ESG performance and cross-border M&A entry. These findings suggest that ESG should not be viewed solely as a legitimacy or reputation device in international expansion. It may also alter firms’ dependence on externally acquired platforms by changing the capabilities available for establishing foreign operations.

title: Peran Intellectual Capital Dalam Membentuk ESG Dan Dampaknya Terhadap Kinerja Keberlanjutan Studi Kasus Pada UKM di Blok M Jakarta
summary: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are among the business sectors facing increasing demands to improve business sustainability through effective internal resource management and the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices. This study aims to analyze the role of Intellectual Capital in shaping ESG practices and its impact on the sustainable performance of SMEs in Blok M, Jakarta. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach involving five informants representing various business sectors, including culinary, fashion, services, and retail. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, direct observations, and documentation, and were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that Intellectual Capital among SMEs in Blok M consists of human capital, relational capital, organizational capital, and structural capital, reflected in entrepreneurs’ experience and skills, relationships with customers and suppliers, task allocation and standard operating procedures, and the use of technologies such as QRIS, cashier applications, and digital record-keeping. ESG practices have been implemented across environmental, social, and governance dimensions, although their implementation remains relatively simple and has not yet been formally integrated into business strategies. Sustainable performance tends to fluctuate but is supported by customer retention, product and service quality, good customer service, innovation, and the ability to adapt to market changes. The findings indicate that Intellectual Capital serves as an internal foundation for shaping ESG practices, which subsequently support the sustainability of SMEs in Blok M, Jakarta

title: THE STRATEGIC ROLE OF GCG IN MODERATING THE EFFECT OF IOS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE ON FIRM VALUE
summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of the investment opportunity set (IOS) and environmental performance on firm value, with good corporate governance (GCG) serving as a moderating variable. The method used in this study is quantitative, utilizing secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports of manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2021–2025. Purposive sampling was applied to determine the sample, resulting in 60 companies. For data analysis, panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) were used. The findings of this study indicate that the IOS and environmental performance have a significant positive influence on firm value. Additionally, GCG enhances the influence of environmental performance on firm value but does not act as a moderator for the impact of the IOS on firm value. These results indicate that investors not only consider a company’s growth potential but also pay attention to environmental responsibility and good governance standards when assessing corporate value. This study contributes to the development of signaling theory and stakeholder theory by reinforcing the aspects of corporate governance and sustainability. The limitations of this study include a sample focused solely on the manufacturing sector and a short observation period. Future research is recommended to expand the sample to other industrial sectors, extend the observation period, and explore alternative moderating variables. Keywords: Investment opportunity set, Environmental performance, Good corporate governance, Firm Value

title: Climate Resilience and Artificial Intelligence in Tourism: A Two-Stage Bibliometric Review and Post Hoc Evidence Audit (2019–2025)
summary: Background: Tourism is among the most climate-sensitive service industries, yet it is simultaneously undergoing rapid digital transformation through artificial intelligence (AI). The overlap and thematic relationships between the retrieved climate resilience and AI-in-tourism literature require empirical description. Methods: We conduct a PRISMA 2020- and PRISMA-S-informed, two-stage bibliometric science mapping review of Scopus and the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection (2019–2025), executed in 2026 and implemented in R (bibliometrix) under the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, complemented by a post hoc-focused full-text evidence audit developed during revision. Stage 1 maps the two parent literatures (N = 9513; Stream A = 2409, Stream B = 7177, shared = 73); Stage 2 is a separately searched exploratory corpus (N = 440) that is not the mathematical intersection of the parent streams. Key findings. The parent fields are large and expanding (24.59% annual growth) but show limited retrieved set overlap: cross-stream overlap is below 1% (0.64% unscreened; 0.77% screened; equivalently 3.03% of Stream A and 1.02% of Stream B), a measure of retrieved set overlap rather than of disciplinary isolation. The retained exploratory corpus has a 53.79% CAGR, and 214 of its 440 records fall outside the screened parent union. Its early relevance screening trail could not be reconstructed, so these findings describe the retained dataset and do not establish field-wide growth or convergence. Post hoc audit. Applying substantive tourism, AI, and climate hazard criteria to 100 assessed full texts identifies 14 studies for an exploratory audit (eight scenario-based, three prediction, and three association), spanning snow, thermal exposure, flooding and landslides, water, and recreation; none demonstrates an evaluated AI-led adaptation benefit. Implications: The findings motivate testing AI-supported climate risk decisions in tourism; they do not demonstrate improved resilience. Non-retrieval of 29 of 129 sought reports (22.5%) and post hoc selection limit the audit.

title: Leveraging Digital Transformation Tools to Enhance Conceptual Understanding in Secondary School Mathematics: A Systematic Review of Pedagogy, Equity and Human Capital Development
summary: Digital transformation tools are increasingly promoted as strategic resources for improving mathematics learning, yet their contribution to conceptual understanding remains uneven across school systems. This systematic literature review examines how dynamic mathematics software, virtual manipulatives, adaptive learning systems, educational games and collaborative digital environments enhance conceptual understanding in secondary school mathematics. Guided by constructivist learning theory, cognitive load theory, socio-cultural theory and technological pedagogical content knowledge, the review synthesises peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2025, supported by PRISMA-informed searching, screening and thematic analysis. The final synthesis shows that digital tools support conceptual understanding when they enable multiple representations, dynamic visualisation, feedback-rich exploration, personalised pathways and mathematical discourse. However, these benefits are conditional rather than automatic. Teacher digital-pedagogical competence, assessment alignment, cognitive design quality, learner language, infrastructure and equitable access mediate whether digital transformation becomes meaningful learning or merely tool substitution. The review contributes to business and social science scholarship by positioning the digital transformation of mathematics as an educational, social equity, and human capital development issue. It argues that secondary mathematics systems require coherent investment in teacher capability, curriculum redesign, responsible data use and inclusive infrastructure. The paper concludes that digital transformation should be governed as a pedagogical and systemic reform process, not as a technological intervention alone.

title: THE ROLE OF DIGITALIZATION IN IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTERNAL CONTROL IN GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS: A LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: Advances in information technology have driven a digital transformation in financial management and government governance. This study aims to analyze the role of digitalization in enhancing the effectiveness of internal controls within government agencies, utilizing a literature review approach. The analysis examines various scholarly articles and academic documents published between 2015 and 2025. The findings indicate that the implementation of integrated information systems—such as e-government, e-budgeting, Financial Management Information Systems (FMIS), the Agency-Level Financial Application System (SAKTI), and Regional Government Information Systems (SIPD)—improves transparency, accountability, the quality of financial reporting, and the effectiveness of monitoring, while also supporting more informed decision-making. Furthermore, digitalization contributes to mitigating the risk of fraud through data integration and process automation. However, its success is contingent upon human resource competence, information technology governance, cybersecurity, and the organization's internal control culture.

title: ESG Rating Improvements and Subsequent Environmental Outcomes: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: Whether ESG rating improvements precede observable environmental progress remains an empirical question. Using 38,430 firm-year observations for Chinese A-share firms covering rating changes from 2010 to 2023, this study examines subsequent recorded environmental penalties, emission-detail availability, and physical-emission changes. Models include firm and industry-by-year fixed effects, with prior regulatory visibility measured through matched key-polluter records. In the Huazheng baseline analysis, a one-standard-deviation increase in aggregate ESG improvement is associated with a 0.45-percentage-point decrease in next-year recorded penalty probability. Aggregate ESG and environmental-pillar improvements are positively associated with subsequent emission-detail availability. Average physical-emission associations are statistically insignificant in the preferred sample of 1130 observations from 363 firms. The negative environmental-pillar interaction under the original regulatory classification persists after selection weighting, while the affirmative-record-group slope is insignificant in the weighted model. Wind retains the positive environmental-pillar observability association, but its penalty and moderation estimates are insignificant. Official-list validation also yields an insignificant environmental-pillar interaction. Raw-quantity classifications yield insignificant associations between ESG improvement and actual reduction. The findings distinguish greater environmental-data visibility from operational emission reduction and show that the environmental interpretation of rating changes depends on the outcome, rating provider, and regulatory classification.

title: Quarterly reporting timeliness as an early signal of reporting and internal control risk
summary: Purpose This paper aims to explore the significance of quarterly report lag as a potential indicator of firms’ annual reporting timeliness and internal control issues, informing policymakers about the incremental value of quarterly reports beyond other well-documented attributes. Design/methodology/approach Following Blankley et al. (2014), the authors use a two-stage approach to estimate a quarterly lag model and then examine the incremental information embedded in the unexplained (abnormal) component of quarterly report lag (AQRL). Findings Based on a sample of the US firms from 2007 to 2023, the authors find that AQRL predicts annual report lag and positively relates to the likelihood of internal control weaknesses. Additional analysis shows that the informational value of AQRL is mainly concentrated among the firms with Big 4 auditors, suggesting that quarterly reporting delays are more informative when audit processes are more standardized and stringent. Originality/value This study responds to the call by Kajüter et al. (2022) that researchers should investigate the impact of quarterly reports on “the time needed to perform the annual audit,” contributing to both interim financial reporting and reporting timeliness literature streams. While prior research mainly focuses on the frequency, content and assurance of quarterly financial reporting, the authors concentrate on the timeliness aspect that conveys useful information about the auditor, the client and the reporting process.

title: PENGARUH INNOVATION CAPABILITIES TERHADAP FIRM PERFORMANCE MELALUI ORGANIZATIONAL AGILITY DAN DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: BUKTI PERUSAHAAN SEKTOR TEKNOLOGI DI BATAM
summary: Abstrak Perkembangan teknologi berperan penting dalam meningkatkan kinerja perusahaan di era digital. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji pengaruh kemampuan inovasi terhadap kinerja perusahaan melalui kelincahan organisasi dan transformasi digital pada perusahaan sektor teknologi di Batam. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling dan jumlah sampel sebanyak 200 responden. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan inovasi berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja perusahaan, kelincahan organisasi, dan transformasi digital. Selain itu, kelincahan organisasi dan transformasi digital juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja perusahaan serta berperan sebagai variabel mediasi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi kemampuan inovasi, kelincahan organisasi, dan transformasi digital mampu meningkatkan kinerja perusahaan. title: ESG-ФАКТОРЫ СТРУКТУРНОЙ МОДЕРНИЗАЦИИ ЭКОНОМИКИ КАЗАХСТАНА: ОТРАСЛЕВЫЕ РАЗЛИЧИЯ И ПРИОРИТЕТЫ РАЗВИТИЯ
summary: Переход к устойчивому промышленному развитию повышает значение экологических, социальных и управленческих факторов структурной модернизации экономики. Цель исследования – выявить отраслевые различия ESG-трансформации базовых отраслей Казахстана и определить приоритетные направления их модернизации. Эмпирическую основу составили официальные статистические данные, материалы Казахстанской фондовой биржи и нормативные документы за 2015–2025 гг. Межотраслевой анализ проведён по показателям 2025 г. для горнодобывающей, обрабатывающей промышленности и энергетики. Предложен метод формирования отраслевого ESG-профиля без объединения показателей в единый рейтинг. Environmental-компонент характеризует природоохранные затраты и экологические инвестиции; Social-компонент – заработную плату, её реальную динамику и производственную безопасность; Governance-компонент – раскрытие ESG-информации, экологический мониторинг и механизмы устойчивого финансирования. Установлена существенная неоднородность отраслевой ESG-трансформации. В энергетике экологические инвестиции составили 87,9% природоохранных затрат и 11,08% капитальных вложений, в обрабатывающей промышленности – 35,2 и 3,18%, в горнодобывающей – 9,8 и 0,52% соответственно. Несмотря на наиболее высокую оплату труда, индекс реальной заработной платы в добывающем секторе составил 98,4%, против 102,5% в обрабатывающей промышленности и 104,4% в энергетике. Результаты обосновывают необходимость дифференцированной ESG-политики: для добывающей отрасли приоритетны технологические экологические инвестиции, для обрабатывающей – зелёные инновации, углубление переработки и цифровизация, для энергетики – декарбонизация, энергоэффективность и обновление инфраструктуры. Предложенный подход позволяет учитывать отраслевую специфику при разработке инструментов государственного регулирования, инвестиционной политики и оценке устойчивости структурных преобразований национальной экономики.

title: Patronage and Accounting Between the Philippines and China, 1733–1797
summary: Abstract Missionary efforts followed the expansion of the Old World’s frontiers, often entwined with trade. This article reviews the accounts of the Franciscan mission in China and of the obras pías of Manila during the eighteenth century to analyse how local conditions and empire-wide structures translated into specific actions on the ground. Through a reconstruction of the economic circumstances, the article explores how the interests of religious orders and merchants became entangled in Manila, showing how this marriage between religion and commerce resulted in a peculiar approach to the financing of the missions, which highlights the versatile nature of Catholic organisation abroad and is reflected in the recordkeeping of the missionaries themselves. The fragmentation and co-optation of multiple interests resulted in greater independence for religious provinces and a method of accounting that prioritised reporting to different patrons over a unified recordkeeping of expenses and sources of income.

title: Biodiversity risk and hotel stock returns: Global evidence from wavelet analysis
summary: This paper aims to examine the dynamic correlation mechanisms between the S&P Global LargeMidCap Biodiversity Index (GBIO) and share prices of nine major global hotel groups. Based on daily data spanning from June 2019 to July 2025, the research utilises advanced econometric methods including wavelet local multiple correlation, wavelet coherence, wavelet quantile correlation, and rolling window wavelet correlation to reveal that biodiversity risk and hotel industry stock returns exhibit significant non-linear, time-varying, and frequency-dependent characteristics. Empirical results demonstrate that the two maintain a strong and stable positive correlation from a long-term investment perspective (exceeding 64 days), with correlation coefficients generally surpassing 0.8, whilst correlation weakens considerably at short-term scales (2–16 days). Cross-regional comparisons reveal that American hotel groups exhibit the strongest positive correlation with the biodiversity index (averaging 0.56), followed by European enterprises (averaging 0.45), with Asian enterprises showing the weakest correlation (averaging 0.27), reflecting the heterogeneity in ESG factor pricing efficiency across different capital markets. This association strengthened significantly following COVID-19, indicating that biodiversity has become a systematic factor influencing the long-term value of the hotel industry in the post-pandemic era. Portfolio optimization analysis reveals that incorporating GBIO into minimum variance portfolios achieves substantial risk reduction of 44–66% in VaR and hedging effectiveness of 68–89%, with optimal GBIO weights consistently around 0.92 or higher. The study provides crucial empirical evidence for investors' ESG investment decisions and policymakers' biodiversity conservation policy design.

title: Factors Affecting Customers' Intention to Use Fintech Payment Services at Joint-Stock Commercial Banks In Vietnam
summary: In the context of the rapid growth of financial technology (Fintech) services in the payment operations of joint-stock commercial banks (JSCBs) in Vietnam, with the value of cashless payments in 2024 exceeding VND 295 quadrillion, this paper aims to systematize, analyze, and comparatively evaluate the factors influencing customers' intention to use Fintech payment services at Vietnamese JSCBs. The paper adopts a desk-research method, synthesizing and comparing domestic and international academic literature on the basis of three underlying theoretical frameworks: the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). The findings show that seven factors - performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, perceived risk, trust, and perceived cost - each play a certain role, with performance expectancy, social influence, and trust showing the highest degree of consensus across the reviewed studies. On this basis, the paper proposes implications for JSCBs in improving the digital experience and building customer trust, and offers policy directions for the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) to promote cashless payment in a sustainable manner.

title: Sharia and Conventional Auditing: A Literature Review and Qualitative Findings From Sharia-Based Businesses
summary: Abstract Sharia and conventional audits share common objectives in providing assurance and assessing organizational accountability. However, they differ in their underlying principles, evaluation criteria, and operational scope. Conventional audits primarily assess the fairness and reliability of financial information in accordance with applicable accounting and auditing standards, whereas Sharia audits additionally evaluate compliance with Islamic principles across business activities, transactions, products, and services. This study examines the distinctions between Sharia and conventional audits and explores the implementation of Sharia auditing beyond Islamic financial institutions, particularly in nonfinancial businesses adopting Sharia principles. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, incorporating a literature review, interviews, discussions, and direct observations of selected businesses in Surabaya, including hospitality establishments, food enterprises, apparel businesses, and educational institutions. The findings reveal variations in the understanding and implementation of Sharia compliance across business sectors and individual establishments. While some businesses demonstrate adherence to halal requirements and Sharia-oriented operational practices, others face difficulties in consistently integrating Islamic principles into their activities. Furthermore, adopting a Sharia label does not necessarily indicate comprehensive compliance with Islamic requirements. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating actual business practices rather than relying solely on formal declarations of Sharia identity. This study contributes to the discussion of Sharia auditing by emphasizing its relevance to nonfinancial business operations and identifying potential inconsistencies between institutional claims and operational practices. Nevertheless, the limited geographical scope and participant involvement restrict the transferability of the findings. Future research should incorporate broader business contexts and develop standardized indicators for assessing Sharia compliance.

title: UM ESTUDO DE CASO SOBRE AS PARCERIAS ENTRE BANCOS E FINTECHS NO MERCADO FINANCEIRO DIGITAL
summary: A partir das parcerias estabelecidas entre bancos e fintechs, o objetivo desta pesquisa é analisar como a parceria entre instituições financeiras de serviços bancários tradicionais e as fintechs promove oportunidades de criação de conhecimento e processos inovativos no mercado financeiro digital. Entende-se que o aprendizado gera conhecimento, cria novas competências e possibilita meios de permitir o crescimento de procedimentos interativos, sustentados pelas relações com outras empresas, nas quais a inovação e a difusão da tecnologia se baseiam. Este trabalho estrutura-se teoricamente na economia do conhecimento, organizações aprendizes, inovação tecnológica no setor financeiro e as parcerias entre bancos e fintechs. A pesquisa é qualitativa e exploratória, os dados foram coletados por meio de entrevistas com os gestores dos bancos tradicionais e das fintechs. Os resultados obtidos demonstram de forma empírica que as parcerias entre bancos tradicionais de médio porte e fintechs promovem novos aprendizados e agilidade, elementos essenciais para impulsionar a inovação e a criação de novos conhecimentos.

title: Digital tools for financial transparency: Challenges, opportunities and prospects
summary: Financial transparency has become a major issue in an increasingly globalized and digitized world. Our work explores the role of digital tools in improving financial transparency, a crucial challenge for companies, governments, and financial institutions. Through a literature review and case studies, our work examines technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), open data platforms (Open Data), and cloud computing. These tools enhance the integrity, traceability, and accessibility of financial data, while reducing the risk of fraud and corruption. For example, blockchain guarantees secure, immutable transactions, while AI detects anomalies and automates auditing processes. Results show that the adoption of these technologies improves corporate governance, boosts stakeholder confidence and facilitates the management of public finances. However, challenges remain, notably in terms of cost, technical skills and data protection. Our work offers recommendations for overcoming these obstacles, such as employee training, regulatory oversight and the promotion of international standards. Digital tools represent a major opportunity to transform financial transparency, provided they are deployed thoughtfully and inclusively. Their adoption could contribute to a more equitable and sustainable management of financial resources, while strengthening trust in economic and political systems.

title: Towards the Digital Transformation of Official Statistics in Latin America and the Caribbean: Evidence on the Use of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence from the 2024–2025 NSO Consultations
summary: This study examines the adoption, use, and institutionalisation of big data and artificial intelligence in official statistics in Latin America and the Caribbean, drawing on the 2024 and 2025 International Consultations conducted with National Statistical Offices. The study combines questionnaire data from 15 responding countries in 2024 and 21 countries and territories in 2025 with qualitative evidence from in-depth interviews. It also proposes the Statistical Innovation Index, a composite indicator designed to approximate differences in the adoption, integration, and institutionalisation of big data and AI across NSOs. Results indicate a gradual consolidation of big data use, although applications remain concentrated in web scraping and satellite imagery, particularly for price, population, environmental, and agricultural statistics. AI adoption remains at an earlier stage: 39% of responding NSOs reported its use, mainly in data processing and other operational tasks. The maturity classification reveals substantial heterogeneity across the region, with most NSOs concentrated in early or emerging stages of statistical innovation. Findings suggest that progress follows a selective process in which exploratory initiatives are gradually filtered into a smaller number of sustainable applications. Institutional capacity, governance, infrastructure, and regional cooperation emerge as key enablers of this process. More broadly, the findings suggest that the transition from exploratory to operational uses of big data and AI reflects an evolving institutional role of NSOs, in which technological innovation is accompanied by new responsibilities for data governance, institutional coordination, and maintaining public trust in official statistics.

title: СТРУКТУРНО-ТЕХНОЛОГИЧЕСКАЯ МОДЕРНИЗАЦИЯ ОТРАСЛЕЙ ПРОМЫШЛЕННОСТИ КАЗАХСТАНА В УСЛОВИЯХ ESG-ТРАНСФОРМАЦИИ: КРИТЕРИИ ОЦЕНКИ
summary: Усиление климатических ограничений, требований к экологической результативности производства и распространение ESG-принципов изменяют подходы к промышленной политике ресурсоёмких экономик. Для Казахстана проблема особенно актуальна вследствие значительной роли добывающего, обрабатывающего и энергетического секторов. Цель исследования заключается в разработке методологического подхода к оценке структурно-технологической модернизации базовых отраслей промышленности с учётом экологических, социальных и управленческих факторов. Использованы официальные статистические данные Казахстана, материалы отраслевых министерств, Всемирного банка и научные исследования за 2015–2025 гг. Предложена пятикомпонентная система критериев, охватывающая структурно-экономические изменения, технологическое обновление, экологическую эффективность, социальную устойчивость и качество управления. Для первоначальной апробации разработан пилотный индекс структурно-технологической модернизации STMI, основанный на нормировании показателей динамики промышленного производства, инвестиций в основной капитал, доли экологических инвестиций в природоохранных расходах и интенсивности экологического инвестирования. По расчётам за 2025 г. значение индекса составило 89,15 пункта для электроэнергетики, газо- и теплоснабжения, 55,00 - для обрабатывающей промышленности, 28,05 - для горнодобывающего сектора и 14,52 - для водоснабжения и обращения с отходами. Эти значения не являются рейтингом ESG-эффективности, а отражают относительную интенсивность наблюдаемых модернизационных процессов в рамках выбранных показателей. Установлено, что рост промышленного производства и капиталовложений сочетается с сохранением значительной энергоёмкости экономики, зависимости от ископаемого топлива и экологической нагрузки. Практическая значимость результатов заключается в возможности совершенствования отраслевого мониторинга модернизации на основе качества технологий, ресурсоэффективности, декарбонизации, человеческого капитала и корпоративного управления. Для дальнейшего развития методики необходимы многолетние сопоставимые данные и расширение социальных и управленческих индикаторов.

title: MENTAL ACCOUNTING AND SHOPPERS’ BEHAVIOR IN SAUDI ARABIA: A QUALITATIVE STUDY
summary: This paper aims to explores the influence of mental accounting on the behavior of shoppers in Saudi Arabia. The review emphasizes the role of this phenomenon in the process of purchasing durable goods in terms of shoppers’ budget, sources of funds, and method of payment. Mental accounting is a concept which implies that individuals classify their expenditures and receipts in a specific way, determining their value in terms other than the interchangeable monetary value. This paper involves a qualitative review study which utilizes a method of narrative and thematic analysis. The framework of this analysis was formed as a synthesis of the existing research on mental accounting and its application to the current trends in electronic payments and financial inclusion in Saudi Arabia. The results of the review found that several factors associated with mental accounting were identified which influence the process of purchase decision-making in Saudi Arabia. The relative importance of a source of funds, the budgetary division of expenditures, the terms of a loan, and the emphasis on the payment process itself have an impact on the shoppers’ assessment of value and justification of expenses. This conclusion highlights the relevance of mental accounting research in terms of electronic payment domination in the Saudi economy, with 85% of all retail payments made electronically in 2025. The analysis also found the impact of substituting cash with card and delayed payments on the mental accounting process, with a possible decrease in the effectiveness of compensatory controls. However, the analysis did not provide sufficient data to support the claim that these factors influence all categories of consumers and all durable goods equally strongly. Finally, the paper concludes that mental accounting research provides a framework for further studies on the phenomenon of mental accounting and consumer behavior in general, with a need for further observations and experiments.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting Pedagogy and SDG Alignment
summary: Despite this interest in artificial intelligence-based accounting pedagogy, the extent to which African scholarship contributes to the field and aligns with sustainable development priorities remains underexplored. This study fills this gap by applying a PRISMA-guided bibliometric analysis alongside an assessment of alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals. Data were drawn from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, yielding a final sample of 148 publications released between 1986 and 2026. Bibliometric techniques, including performance analysis, Bradford’s Law, Lotka’s Law, co-authorship mapping, thematic analysis and conceptual structure mapping, were employed using the Bibliometrix R package. The findings point to a fast-growing research area with an annual growth rate of 5.34%, in which publication output has risen sharply since 2022, following the emergence of generative AI technologies. Research productivity and citation impact remain heavily concentrated in developed economies, particularly the United States, Australia and the United Kingdom, while African contributions are comparatively limited and largely driven by South Africa. Thematic analysis identifies artificial intelligence, accounting education, data analytics, skills development and higher education as dominant research clusters. Furthermore, the study from African researchers demonstrates substantial implicit alignment with SDG 4 and SDG 9. However, explicit integration of SDG frameworks within the literature remains limited. The study concludes that although African scholarship is contributing meaningfully to AI-driven educational innovation, greater investment in research capacity, digital infrastructure, international collaboration, and SDG-orientated scholarship is required to strengthen the continent’s influence in the global accounting education discourse and to support sustainable education.

title: Determinants of firms’ motivation for environmental management accounting
summary: Environmental management accounting (EMA) has become increasingly important as firms face growing expectations to improve environmental performance while maintaining competitiveness (Schaltegger & Burritt, 2017; Doan et al., 2023; Elhossade et al., 2022). Despite its recognized benefits, EMA implementation remains uneven in many emerging economies, including Vietnam. This study examines factors associated with firms’ motivation to implement EMA among Vietnamese enterprises that have implemented or are piloting EMA practices. Drawing on institutional theory, stakeholder theory, the resource-based view (RBV), and contingency theory, the study investigates the roles of environmental legal regulations, stakeholder pressure, leadership commitment, accounting staff capabilities, and industry characteristics. Survey data were collected from 243 respondents and analyzed using reliability testing, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), and multiple regression. The results indicate that all five factors are positively associated with firms’ motivation to implement EMA. Environmental legal regulations exhibit the strongest association, followed by stakeholder pressure, leadership commitment, accounting staff capabilities, and industry characteristics. The findings suggest that external pressures play a more prominent role than internal organizational conditions in shaping EMA motivation. The study provides practical implications for policymakers and managers seeking to promote broader EMA implementation.

title: Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models
summary: Single-cell perturbation models are increasingly assessed for both predictive performance and calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. We constructed such an evaluation harness (two datasets, Norman 2019 and Replogle 2022; four split types over six dataset-split combinations; three models, scVI, CPA and a linear Ridge baseline; three uncertainty quantification methods, MC dropout, quantile regression and split conformal prediction) and then audited it against null baselines it had never included. Most of its headline results measure something other than what their metric names claim. The harness supplied each test cell to the model as input and then scored the model on reproducing that same cell's expression, so an identity predictor returning the input unchanged attains a perturbation-effect correlation of 1.0 on all six splits: any model given the target cell is measured against this echo ceiling rather than against a null. Against a constant train-mean predictor, scVI wins on 99.7% of Norman cells but only 0.2% of Replogle cells. One split held out sequencing batches rather than perturbations; another scores no genuinely novel perturbation after label collapse; unseen perturbations are silently replaced with a negative-control sentinel at inference; and the most convention-sensitive decision-value entry moves 29.2 percentage points under a library-size convention that changes that row's all-gene MSE by 0.01%. Because a validation budget is spent on a ranked shortlist rather than on a marginal interval, we also score each uncertainty signal by the DE-gene error it avoids in the top k: the worst-calibrated method is the best ranker, and a benchmark reporting only coverage orders the two backwards. We document six failure modes, each with its mechanism, the diagnostic that exposes it, and a detection procedure transferable to other harnesses. One result survives, with a boundary condition: split-conformal coverage calibrated on K562 residuals under-covers on RPE1 (0.900 to 0.847), and marginal coverage at the nominal 0.900 is compatible with covering 0.271 to 0.342 of the DE-gene intervals a prioritization decision would rest on. We continue to recommend conformal prediction, recalibrated per cellular context and reported per gene set rather than marginally.

title: Literasi Keuangan Syariah Dan Partisipasi Masyarakat Dalam Pasar Modal Syariah: Studi Literatur
summary: Sharia financial literacy is a crucial factor in enhancing public understanding of Sharia financial products and services, including the Sharia capital market. However, public participation in the Indonesian Sharia capital market remains relatively low, despite its immense development potential. This study aims to examine the role of Sharia financial literacy in increasing public participation in the Sharia capital market. A library research method with a descriptive-qualitative approach was employed. Data were gathered from various secondary sources—such as books, scholarly journals, articles, and official publications—pertaining to Sharia financial literacy and the Sharia capital market. Content analysis was used to analyze the data by identifying, comparing, and interpreting relevant research findings. The results indicate that Sharia financial literacy plays a significant role in enhancing public knowledge, confidence, and the ability to make investment decisions in accordance with Sharia principles. In addition to Sharia financial literacy, public participation is also influenced by factors such as education level, income, investment motivation, ease of technological access, risk perception, and trust in Sharia financial institutions. Therefore, efforts to improve Sharia financial literacy through continuous education and outreach must be sustained to boost public participation in the Sharia capital market and support national economic growth.

title: ESG Score and Firm Value: The Role of the Institutional Context—A Comparative Analysis of the United States and the European Union
summary: The relationship between ESG performance and firm value is contested and appears to depend on context. This study asks whether that relationship differs between the United States and the European Union, two mature markets that differ primarily in the extent to which sustainability disclosure is mandated. Firm fixed-effects panel regressions are estimated on LSEG (Refinitiv) data for 2016–2024, covering 874 firms and 5848 firm-year observations, with firm value measured by winsorized Tobin’s Q in levels. Among U.S. firms, the estimated association is indistinguishable from zero until 2022 and positive and significant in 2023; among EU firms, it is not significant in any year. The joint hypothesis that the regional differentials are zero in every year is rejected and remains rejected under every robustness check, including the logarithm of Enterprise Value, a lagged ESG score and alternative control sets; the test concerns the period as a whole and does not identify individual years. Functional-form criteria retain linearity, and the turning point implied by a quadratic specification cannot be located on the ESG scale. A direct test of equality across sectors is weak. Institutional context is proxied by region; regulatory stringency and market sentiment are not measured, so the mechanism is not tested.

title: Stakeholder-driven ESG perceptions and employee willingness to engage in sustainable practices: evidence from hospitality businesses
summary: Purpose This study examined how employees' perceptions of environmental, social and governance (ESG) initiatives impacted their willingness to engage in ESG practices in the hospitality industry. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 396 full-time employees working in hospitality businesses in Thailand to test the study's hypotheses using partial least squares structural equation modelling, necessary condition analysis (NCA), and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA). Findings The social and governance dimensions of ESG perceptions significantly enhanced perceived ESG benefits, while the environmental dimension did not yield a direct effect. Surprisingly, employee awareness of ESG weakened the relationship between perceived benefits and willingness to engage, suggesting that cognitive dissonance or scepticism may emerge at higher awareness levels. The results of the NCA indicated that the social and governance dimensions show bottleneck levels, whereas the environmental dimension had negligible necessity effects on perceived ESG benefits. Practical implications The study recommends that hospitality managers prioritise governance and social practices before they institutionalise ethical reporting structures. It supports the idea that managers should reframe environmental initiatives when building firms that operate in environmentally friendly ways. Originality/value The study contributes to the hospitality literature by demonstrating how ESG initiatives affect employee behaviour, drawing on stakeholder theory and social exchange theory. In addition, the integration of multimethod analyses provides valuable insights for the hospitality industry.

title: Machine-Learning-Guided Control Selection in ESG–Performance Models: Evidence from a Global Firm Panel
summary: This study examines the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and firm financial performance while considering the moderating role of institutional quality and the sensitivity of the results to control-variable selection. The analysis uses 68,244 firm-year observations for 6204 listed firms across developed and developing economies between 2011 and 2021. Firm performance is measured using Tobin’s Q, return on assets (ROA), and return on equity (ROE), while ESG is examined through its aggregate score and its environmental, social, and governance pillars. We use Random Forest to rank candidate controls, and we combine its rankings with multicollinearity diagnostics. Conventional full-control and Random Forest-informed specifications are then compared using OLS and quantile regressions. The results show that control selection materially affects the magnitude, direction, and statistical significance of the estimated ESG coefficients. Although there are clear relationships between ESG and performance variables in the baseline model, they become statistically insignificant when using the firm-fixed effects models, implying that the findings arise mainly from the persistent difference between firms rather than within-firm ESG performance. In addition, market responses are more selective: the Social pillar is positively associated with Tobin’s Q, whereas the Environmental pillar is negatively valued in several specifications. Institutional moderation also varies across ESG pillars, governance dimensions, performance measures, and quantiles. Government Effectiveness and Rule of Law provide the most consistent evidence of positive moderation for the aggregate ESG–Tobin’s Q relationship, while the evidence is weaker or less stable for ROA and ROE. Our findings demonstrate that the financial relevance of ESG is context-dependent and sensitive to empirical model specification.

title: Digital Government and Corporate Green Total Factor Productivity: Evidence from Chinese Listed Industrial Firms
summary: Industrial sustainability depends on cleaner production and more efficient resource use. This study examines whether local digital government development is associated with faster growth in the green total factor productivity of industrial firms, and which corporate decisions change alongside it. We use annual data on Chinese listed industrial firms from 2017 to 2023. Matching annual corporate records to a city-level digital government index, we find that a one standard deviation increase in the index raises the annual green productivity growth index by 0.0253, equivalent to 16.6% of its standard deviation. Two mechanisms are at work. Digital government promotes green innovation: green invention applications become more frequent and account for a larger share of green patent applications. It also disciplines investment: the capital expenditure rate declines and investment deviation narrows, consistent with less overinvestment. The relationship is stronger with greater telecommunications activity, broader financial service coverage, higher earnings retention, and more stable management, and weaker with greater stock forum sentiment dispersion. Digital public services thus support sustainable industrial transformation through green innovation and more efficient capital allocation, linking digital government policy to the cleaner production and resource efficiency goals of sustainable development.
